At the last line, if you can't take the pair in front of you, the scrolling will move your block out and the game will end.

210678.overview: In Bug Squish the player has to protect their own arm from blood-sucking insects. Using a fly-swatter (controlled by the mouse or a touch screen) they need to be squished before they suck you dry. There are 32 waves, with various bug types, and occasional "extra blood" and score multiplier bonuses. It is based on the Macintosh shareware game Blood Suckers.

210681.overview:
Biniax 2 is the sequel to the puzzle game Biniax. It keeps the core puzzle mechanics and expands mainly through new game modes. The Arcade mode is the closest to the original version. It is an endless game on a fixed-screen board where blocks, made up out of two differently coloured pieces each, gradually drop down over the entire width of a field. The player controls a single piece with one colour and can freely move it around the board as long as there is room.

The second game mode is the Tactic mode. It is a slower puzzle mode where only a limited amount of moves are available to prevent the rows from constantly reaching the bottom. 

The final mode is the competitive multiplayer mode with local multiplayer for two players simultaneously, each controlling a piece on the same screen

210701.overview:
The year is 1993. The rock star Axel Pose is on the peak of his success and in celebration of his new album, a radio station organizes a lottery. Answer five question about this album and win a meeting with Axel Pose. This game is based on the real-life band Guns 'n' Roses and their front man Axl Rose. As a big fan, you are of course trying to buy the album immediately - but it is not as easy as it seems...

As a promotional game, Backstage is neither long nor complicated. With a standard point-and-click interface you solve puzzles and speak to people. During the whole game, an advertising message is clearly delivered urging the player to join Lifeclub, a real buyer's club for purchasing products at discounted prices.

210702.overview: Bacman is a Pac-Man clone with slightly upgraded graphics compared to the original.

210715.overview: Baffle is a puzzle game where your goal is to find as many words where the letters are connected to each others as possible within the limited time frame. When the time expires, you'll see all the words you missed.

210717.overview:
The premise of Baldies is similar to many real-time strategy games. You start with a limited number of Baldies with which you construct buildings, increase your population, and create the necessary instruments of war. There are four classes of Baldies--builders, scientists, soldiers, and workers/breeders. Structures include small, medium, large, and huge houses as well as science labs and barracks. Each building has specific properties that assist in your destruction of the enemy.

Baldies originally started as a project intended for the Amiga platforms, but despite becoming a small hit for a number of platforms and later followed by a sequel "Skullcaps", it was never released for Amiga. A beta version from 1993 is the only version ever seen on the platform.

210718.overview: Collect the lost games over 20 levels. Baldy is a platform game, written using AMOS and involves controlling your man as he navigates fixed platforms on screen. Each level introduces different enemies and patterns to avoid and selected platforms cannot be used. Each level has a set number of disks to collect before moving to the next one.

210719.overview: Ball Lightning is an action puzzler. The protagonist is a bouncy ball with hands. You move around collecting and using items to solve the various puzzles thrown in your way.

210721.overview:
Bally II is a single player, keyboard controlled, shareware game from Germany.

The game area is a large rectangle within which are a number of bouncing balls, very small and moving very fast. The player has to draw lines on the screen and section off areas of the screen. A life is lost if a bouncing ball comes into contact with a line that is being drawn.

210722.overview:
Bally V is one in the series of Qix clones mostly distributed on the gaming magazine cover disks at the time. The objective is to draw lines that close off parts of the screen to fill in a set amount of the playfield. Once the percentage is set you move on to the next level. If any of the enemies flying around touches your line while being drawn, you'll lose a life.

What sets the Bally series from the other Qix clones are the graphics: both you and the enemies are single pixels.

210723.overview:
Balls is a clone of a Pollymorph, a single-player colour-matching puzzle game.

In this game the player controls a small ball that can be used move other balls around. When two same-coloured balls meet they disappear. The game objective is to clear the game area by pushing balls of the same colour together. The number1 of balls and the complexity of the game area increases as the player progresses through the game.

210725.overview: Probably inspired by Death Sword/Barbarian, Bamber's Fighting Clone is a one- or two-player fighting game where two sword-wielding barbarians fight it out on an arena till death do them apart.

210727.overview: The basic concept of the game is simple: you have to guide the ball around the play area destroying all the pods, then head for the exit before the time runs out by placing deflectors around the field. Once placed the deflectors cannot be removed, but their orientation can be altered. There's also various tokens lying around which will either hinder or help you by altering the ball speed, destroying it, changing the remaining time or turning it indestructable, giving it the ability to break through the walls.

210755.overview: Bambino fait un Puzzle is a jigsaw game aimed at pre-school children 3-8 years old. AUTHORS: Pierre DOISSOT-Regis LORIN AH-Gerard MAURY Bambinours, the plavfal bear, proposes that you put the 8, 9, 12 or 16 pieces of a puzzle (amongst the 20 at hand) which you can choose back into their place.

210757.overview: Banana Islands is a platform game inpired by the late and great Rainbow Islands where you're a monkey that has an ability to shoot and climb over bananas to reach hard-to-reach locations.

210758.overview: Bandit is a straigh-up One-Armed Bandit gambling simulator featuring a three reel setup and multiple betting lines. This was published commercially and published by both Intersoft (Harald Muller) and Schatztruhe in 1995.

210760.overview: Bandit Mania is a compilation of three different slot machine variations. In addition to the slot machines, one of the variations has multiple arcade games built-in; you get to play familiar games like Snake or Minesweeper in order to maximize your winnings.

210766.overview:
Pang is a hack of Poing, itself a variation of Breakout. In this adaptation the game is played from left to right. Your task is not to eliminate every block, but to gain access to the back wall, by removing the blocks in front of it, and hit it 10 times, at which point you can go through it onto the next screen.

Sets of 8 screens are grouped together, and when you lose the ball on that level you get hurtled back through the previous ones at high speed. If you manage to catch the ball on one of them, you can continue from that level, trying to force the ball back through the end of the level, and get back to where you were.

210770.overview: Banger Racers is a multiplayer-only top-down racing game for 2-4 players.

210819.overview: Batdog is a platform game with some light puzzle elements. The protagonist starts with no run and jump power.  Collecting all the gold rings in each stage will complete the level while collecting the special gems is required to score enough points to enter the bonus pinball-type levels that gets you new powers required to beat the boss.

210900.overview: Battle Pong is a fun modern take on the classic Pong. As the match continues, the board starts to fill with various powerups. They might expand or shrink your paddle, reverse the controls or change the direction of the ball. Should the game still continue, an extra paddle will appear to the middle, possibly intervening with your or your opponent's shot.

210931.overview: Battle Space is a shareware space shooter, first game of Akson Software. The Player takes the role of a spaceship pilot named Roger Ptak, providing transports escorting services. Babylonian system was attacked by Vandal race. The pilot receives a proposal to join a defensive army in exchange for an intergalactic battleship and a large sum of money. The player controls the ship, fighting off wave after wave of enemy attacks. The ship may be moved right or left, fire the missiles, or launch a single mine. The enemies attack and move in different ways, including attacking from the bottom of the screen. They have different shield resistance and firepower. The Power-ups are marked as wings with various colors, depending on what they add, including additional ship, extra shields, and mines or increased firepower.

210932.overview: Battle Tec is a puzzle game where your goal is to make all the buttons on the board turn red. There are five colors in total. When you click one, the neighboring buttons will also change their color in a sequential order visible on the top of the screen. As a surprising game mechanism there's no time limit; instead it's replaced by a WWI fighter flying around, coming towards your mouse cursor at all times. If it catches you it's game over; if you manage to turn all the buttons the right color before that, the fighter explodes and on to the next level you go.

211010.overview:
In the far future of 2010, many years after World Word 3, flying cars and wristwatch TVs are commonplace and the human race has abolished its armies, now living a peaceful existence.

But one day a UFO descends from the skies. Its cargo, an alien race of machines seeking a new world after their own was destroyed by a supernova. The defenceless humans are powerless against the warmongering machines and promptly surrender to their mechanical overlords and their diabolical leader, The Animator.

All hope is lost until one day a strange misshapen figure walks out of the nuclear wastelands. A genetic cocktail of lifeforms, it is half man, half baked bean. It is known as... Bean.

211011.overview: How would you like to play the latest Amiga port of a very fine Atari/Amstrad game first released in the early 90's by the well known company Ubisoft? Well now you can with Back to the Golden age; An Arcade, Action sword fighting game where you can explore rooms, castles and dungeons all the while fighting knights, warriors and other strange beasts that lurk in the next screen. What's more... You can buy supplies, find loot and even cast spells, it's a grand game indeed with cool animation, fighting sequences and plenty of gameplay that will keep you occupied for ages.

211012.overview:
Bubblestones 2 is a Puzzle Bobble/Bust a move clone on the Amiga from Guy Massonanve

This is my first ever play of the game.

Taken from the readme.

- AGA, 256 colors
- possibility to change the look of the game. (Read the doc)
- keyboard support
- new game mode : HOT
- many improvement for best gameplay
- English docs

211013.overview:
A new puzzle game made in AMOS by Colin Vella;
was originally called Block Head until we found the name was already taken :/
I contributed the in-game musics and am actually working on main tune
(the actual title tune is a placeholder put by Colin)

Game is still in progress so try to follow the thread for updates

Note: Does not work on stock A500 setup, A1200 config recommended

211109.overview: BattleDuel is an artillery game. Two players fight against each other with cannons placed in a windy mountainous landscape. To hit the other they change the powder and angle of the cannons. A duel is finished when one of the cannons is totally destroyed.

211206.overview:
Rescue Esmeralda from the evil clutches of Baldric the Guardsman by leaping over various obstacles and bead-butting the bell at the end of each of the 40 screens. 

While featuring some new bells and whistles, the game is based on Ocean's 1983 Hunchback.

211207.overview:
BattleScape is a turn-based strategy game in which two teams struggle to annihilate each other on a randomly generated world. 

Each team begins with a single builder. From this the player must create a nation complete with agricultural and economic systems, people, factories and research laboratories in order to develop the power needed to defeat an equally determined enemy.

211209.overview:
BattleStar is a fun text-based adventure game, reminiscent of Zork and Adventure. You start out on a space ship under attack and must get off and back to the planet. It was originally written for mainframes back in 1979 and later ported to most platforms, including Amiga.

Battlestar is described as a 'stellar-tropical adventure game' in the source code header. You initially find yourself in in a battlestar that is under attack and must make your escape. However, there are many useful items in the battlestar that you may need before you escape, but only so many turns before it explodes.

Battlestar is interesting among text adventures in that it tracks the current player orientation and updates the directions based on the current facing. For example, entering the room on the 'right', would result in a direction of 'behind' for leaving the room again. Re-entering the room would then be 'behind' when back in the corridor. Absolute directions (N,S,E,W) are possible, but only when a compass is found.

211268.overview: A ninja fighting clone of Bad Dues Vs Dragon Ninja and was developed using the Amiga game creation software RedPill.

211272.overview: Biker Babe from Barbados is an Amiga platformer shoot'em up game released in 1995. This horizontal shooter was inspired by William Nolan'sgame Bock Tooth Bob and depicts senseless acts of violence.

211298.overview: Baum is a cave shooter for two players. It's the only game developed by  Noxious, otherwise known for their demo releases. The goal is to move through the maze with your spaceship till you find the other player and shoot them until they explode.

211300.overview:
In Bazza 'n' Runt, the player takes the role of Bazza in search for Old Man Misty who is said to hold the knowledge of the perfect platformer storyline. Which is appropriate, because this game is a series of one-screen platformer levels.

To finish a level, a certain amount of targets need be destroyed with bombs. Bazza has a limited amount with him which can be dropped and explode after a few seconds. However, Bazza should be gone by then because the bombs are deadly to him, too (except when the option was disabled in the options). The good news is that the bombs also kill the enemies which wander around the levels on fixed routes. When Bazza runs out of bombs, he needs to get new ones by catching icons which constantly fall from the sky. In addition, there are fruits (bonus points for the high-score) and letters to catch. When Bazza caught enough letters, he gets to participate in a mini game after finishing the current level. There are also other power-ups which, for example, freeze all enemies.

The two-player mode is competitive. Both players, the second one taking control of Runt, try to destroy the most targets. I this mode, there are special power-ups which have negative consequences for the other player character, e.g. removing all bombs.

211306.overview: Beasties is a copy of Team 17's popular turned-based artillery game Worms. You move cute creatures over destructable terrain and try to hit your opponents with a selection of weapons before they can eliminate you.

211307.overview: Beat It is a board game/puzzler where your goal is to remove all pieces from the board by jumping over them. You can only jump over a piece when two pieces are next to each other and there's an empty space after them to jump into.

211310.overview: Breaking the Lawn is a clone of the 1983 Llamasoft game Hover Bovver, and also a fan-made tribute to the notorious 1990s animated TV series Beavis & Butt-Head. The game can be played with 1 or 2 players, and uses joystick controls. Each screen shows a large garden from high above, with grass, flowers and water features. You control either Beavis or Butt-Head, and you have a lawn mower. Your goal is to mow everything on the screen, before you can move on to the next garden. You must avoid falling in the water, and there is also an angry dog and an angrier gardener that you will need to avoid.

211311.overview: Beavis & Butthead Domino is game for one or two players which apparently simulates Beavis & Butthead playing the dominoes. Outside of the sound samples from the series, the game is a straight-up domino board game.

211312.overview:
BeBop 'n Drop is a real-time puzzle game and an enhanced commercial release of the shareware game Obsess-O-Matic. The object is to fit the falling playing cards together to form complete horizontal rows, which will then disappear off the bottom of the board. 

The game was republished in early 1993, including further enhancements, notably a built-in editor allowing players to create their own piece sets, change sound sets, design their own playing boards or alter the levels provided.

211313.overview:
The aim of Beetle is to reach the top of the garden wall before the green beetle. The wall consists of a hundred levels, each full of baddies that will glady eat you, and baby grubs that have to be collected. Once all the grubs are safe, the teleporter will be activated and you can proceed onto the next level. You have to beat the game within 40 minutes. 

Apart from the platforming, there are bonus levels with different gameplay taken from popular titles like Pang and Obscure Blitz.

211425.overview:
Blain Home is a platform game, very arcade where you control Blain in a very special mission, destroy gas containers that have been hidden in various places in various locations. To do this you have a minigum 134 and your skills to avoid all the dangers arising from the mission.

Where did this game come from? Since the Predator movie was released in the late 1980s, it is a topic that has often come up in conversations with many friends, we repeat phrases, comment on scenes and speculate about the characters. One of the most attractive to us is Blain and his automatic machine gun. In addition to this weapon, it has a macho man's arsenal that would give any defender of current feminism goosebumps. Phrases like: Here we go, bastards. I don't have time to bleed and of course that great phrase of keep it up and you will become sexual Tyrannosaurus. They have accompanied us throughout our lives, endorsing them to friends as soon as an occasion called for it and receiving them equally. Blain had his friend inseparable from him Mac from him who dedicated that great phrase to him: Blain, Blain. Does it remind you of home? I guess both friends missed home, hence the game's title Blain Home. Referring to the fact that when Blain finishes his mission he goes to his home.

211468.overview: This is a concentration-demanding puzzle-deconstruction game in the fashion of MahJong and Lin-Wus Challenge. You pick pairs systematically from a large set of tiles and respect certain rules of alignment or accessibility. BlitzWays is an oldschool puzzle game in the style of Mahjong or Lin-Wu's Challenge. The game was written for the Amiga 500, one of the most popular computers of the 90's, made by Commodore Business Machines, who also created the C64. The Amiga series of computers has a cult following among retro-computer enthusiasts, and many games and demos are still being created for it, to this day.

211512.overview:
Another Bomb Jack clone. The problem with this version is the short time you have on all levels. Some of them can't even be completed without picking up bonus items (time bonus, speedup or a key). The bonus items are randomly dropped. So you really need to have luck to get them. Very lame level design. Wonder if the author took his time to play test the levels before release.

60 levels in this one? Well, there is actually only 20. Level 21-40 and 41-60 has the same level design as level 1-20. They are just slightly harder. You must play all 60 levels to play the last one (level 61).

211713.overview: A puzzle game created by Generation X coder Paul Nordovics and released in 1994.

211722.overview: This side scrolling beat 'em up puts you in control of Brus on a rescue mission to save your kidnapped girlfriend from a criminal organization, hell bent on stopping you from entering the martial arts tournament.

211772.overview: A bloody mana-y-mano, head to head fighting game created by Eric Park in AMOS. More fun than Amiga's version of Street Fighter 2, Dangerous Streets and Rise of the Robots all put together.

211807.overview: Buzzy full release was released with level editor, this slick platformer (with documentation written entirely in French) has you in the role of Buzzy, who along with his family has been abducted by aliens in the middle of a dark and stormy night and has been turned into a bouncing ball for their amusement.  You awake on a strange island and you must find your family by traveling through this curious place, collecting lollipops and eating mushrooms along the way. Along the way you will also find helpful trampolines to get the most out of your bounce.

211824.overview: Written in AMOS Professional. Game ideas by Patrik & Tor Jansson. Coding by Patrik Jansson. Graphics by Tor & Patrik Jansson. Title music by Mark Salud, additional music/FMV sound by Ruben Monteiro and sound FX/FMV sound by Patrik Jansson. Based on the strategy pencil and paper or the popular  Milton Bradley board game, but for 4 possible players in one game.

211830.overview: It is two years after Botss 2. President Gilbert Bates is dead. Zackaria is presumed gone. The EDF becomes less vigilant. Earth Force space station Z35 is attacked. The five pilots who fought Zackaria before were not onboard the station when the attack came. The station is quickly overwhelmed. Mars Force DRAGON jumps into Earth Force space attacking immediately. The EDF tries valiantly but cannot hold. DRAGON uses the antimatter cannon and the defenses are obliterated, save a handful of fighters.  With the station taken and the crew mind-probed, the strike to earth has begun. Only you can save us, our last line of defense.

211869.overview:
The precursor to Blake Stone: Planet Strike also released for the Amiga in 2017. Aliens of Gold, the first game in the Blake Stone series, pits the space-age British secret agent against Dr. Pyrus Goldfire; a madman bent on world domination. Using a mastery of genetic engineering and a tremendous reserve of wealth, Dr. Goldfire intends to unleash a mutant army upon the Earth.

The first chapter begins in Goldfire's S.T.A.R. Institute headquarters building. Each level has Blake fighting through guards to find an elevator keycard for the next level. Dr. Goldfire will personally appear along the way to fire shots at Blake, and his genetic creations also pose a tough challenge. Each chapter lasts 10 levels, and brings Blake closer to reaching Goldfire, only to have the mad doctor escape to a new installation in his network, and the start of a new chapter.

211925.overview: Balder's Grove is an Amiga boulder dash arcade game released in 1994 where two players can play simultaneously.

211926.overview: Four different brushes are battling to paint more of the canvas than their enemies! A multiplayer fun game for up to 4 simultaneous players!

211927.overview: You've heard of miniature golf, this is the same idea but with pool! Created by Federico Spinola, Alessandro Scardovi, and Stefano Luciani in 1991.

211928.overview: This 2D fixed-screen shooter was released on a cover disk: The One in June 1993. The frenzy of non-stop action, featuring 148 breeds of evil alien vermin intent upon your destruction.

211929.overview: BLOCKY SKIES includes 10 levels of arcade puzzler and 3 songs by Simone "JMD" Bernacchia. The game is highly original. Minimalistic in design, but well professionally programmed. And hella addictive!

211930.overview:
This time we have Blood ‘N’ Bullets, Created in 1989 by Sensible Software, (This Game was also given away with special version of SEUCK distributed with CU Amiga Magazine)

This is kinda similar to Commando, where you have to shoot soldiers, and even soldiers on motorcycles/motorbikes in order to rack up plenty of points

There are also soldiers who walk around placing bombs in order to kill you, as well as Tanks what fire rounds across the screen, and even the soldiers themselves move in all directions firing bullets at you, along with ones who pop out of the water and shoot, before diving back underneath

At the end of the levels, You have a static screen, and several enemies will come to pop you off if you are not quick enough to avoid the bullets

Plenty of Pickups around too, which are shown as Medals, and when picked up add to your score in the bottom middle

211931.overview: A flappy bird clone and a challenging one, set in space and the enemies shoot at you. Two players can play simultaneously.

211932.overview: This little clone of Puzzle Bobble was created with ripped graphic elements from a PC clone. Sound, music and explosions were added and a working game was put together in a few weeks. It was released to the world a year later. Enjoy!

211933.overview: Bounce around the level to pick up all the stars without hitting a blocking item. Get the highest score possible.

211934.overview: Bouncing balls run in the blood of the Amiga from the start. It should be no surprise that there are bouncy creatures aplenty in the Amiga gamespace. This PD\Freeware game by Ben Wyatt is one of them, written in AMOS. The game comes with the level editor.

211935.overview: An Arkanoid style game created by Jean-Baptiste Bolcato (Starsky) and released in 1997. In it hitting certain blocks will release capsules that when caught offer power ups when caught. Some will advance you to the next level, some contain disadvantageous items like speeding up the ball or decreasing the size of the bat you must catch\hit the ball with.

211988.overview: Inspired by the classic "H.E.R.O." game, "BioJet" is a variation of the fly/dodge in what some would call a flying platformer and other would characterize as a labyrinth game.

211989.overview: Peg those blasted birds! Knock them out of the sky and try not to be hit by their droppings, unless you are into that sort of thing. Upgrade your weapon and clear the skies. Turn the world into your no fly zone.

211991.overview:
Twenty levels of multi-player mayhem. Full version also contains a level editor to make your own games. The aim of the game is simple. You are a blob who must fight for your life in an arena against other blobs. To kill the other blobs you must jump onto their eyes and squash them. Up to three blobs may fight in the arena at once. The game allows for two players on joysticks and one player on keys. The controls are simple:
  left and right move you left and right and fire makes you jump. If you hold down fire you can jump higher than if you tap it. When you die, the number of lives you have decreases. When your lives reach zero you are out of the game. The game continues until only one blob is left in the arena. After you die, if you have lives remaining, you are teleported back into the arena to continue fighting. You will be invincible for a short while.

211992.overview: A game created by Graham Humphrey back in 2004 in Blitz Basic, it contains over 56 levels. This was his first game he created for the Amiga. Graham is still active in the community and creating new games.

211993.overview: This tricky platformer has 100 levels of fun and challenge for you as you control a grasshopper and jump your way around the underground cavern, avoiding all manner of baddies and ghosts.

212054.overview: Othello for up to four players at once, a game by Andrew Crowe of Manta Soft, released in 1998.

212055.overview:
This game is made by the same guy that created Backbone (game creator software). Also, the creator of Hanger 18 and Turtleminator. 
This game, however, is not a Backbone game. It's created in AMOS. The object of Blobby is to rescue all of his friends from the Big Nasty Monster Lair and retrieve his football which he lost the other day.

212056.overview: Quite the surprise when suddenly the drunk driving came up in what looked up until that point like a predictable events-based party game with events like Barrel Weightlifting and Beer Shooting. A substantial amount of effort went into it even though it was probably played only by drunk sceners at The Party 1994 and by not many people afterwards.

212151.overview: Bounce on the points, follow the rules of the board to clear everything out and get to the exit. Nice jumping and skill game with a ball. This must be transported over a dismembered board. But there are still many enemies who want to prevent that...

212257.overview: Santa doesn't want to work today, he wants a few drinks. The toys, however, don't want to let him. He's a mean drunk. Help Santa collect the gold coins so he can have a Jolly Christmas eve at home. If you collect all the coins on all 5 levels Santa can have a jolly time. Plus these damn kids have too many toys.

212259.overview: Shooter created with AMOS by Lee C. Wilson of delta9. Blast our way through no less than 50 levels of alien action. Simply blast everything that moves. During the game, aliens will drop power crystals that can be collected by moving the yellow rectangle at the top of the screen. Weapons can be changed out during play. Click P to catch a breath. Nice little game, quick and quite addictive.

212260.overview: Graphics ripped straight out of Yoshi's Island and what was added looks amateurish at best. The player sprites have too few frames of animation. Despite the omnipresence of ladders in the levels, there is no animation for ladder climbing, so Blip and Blop awkwardly "wiggle" up and down when they use them. On the plus side, the background music is quite good and the game is at least playable, brief as it is. I guess there was a bit of a novelty factor in seeing Nintendo and Studio Peyo characters brutally exploded and dismembered. Too me, it looks childish. In 2004, an updated and expanded version of Blip & Blop was released for Windows.

212376.overview: A game written in Amos by Alain Bonney where you duel on the ocean against a ship controlled by the computer.

212377.overview: BallMaster is a puzzle game with a simple basic idea and (hopefully) addictive gameplay. It is based on an old game named Logical. This game tries to bring its idea to newer Amiga hardware and also tries to extend the original game with some new ideas. Game contains source code. It has 100 levels of play and password access every 5 levels. It was released on the Amiga Classix 3 compilation.

212384.overview: A version of the classic board game for up to 4 players. Players get 9 ships to arrange on the game board and the game proceeds by otherwise normal rules. This homebrew game by Bryan stu and Bill was not released to the public domain.

212385.overview:
Battle of the Stink Beetles is a simple tank battle game where the tanks are beetles (chosen from a selection of four) and the ammunition is spit. It's a two player only affair set in one of a choice of six arenas (very Micro Machines style) in which the two combatants trundle about trying to spit at each other. 

Each beetle also has a set number of mines to drop (once you've picked them from the options menu) in an attempt to harm the other fella and new supplies are delivered by a butterfly 'airforce'. You can even find yourself running from enemy bumblebee 'bombers'. 

It's mad stuff! 

What's most impressive with this game though is just how tactical the play becomes. You can't just bimble about firing left, right and centre, you've got to think about what you're doing and make full use of whatever landscape features there are - even to the point of hiding 


under balls of dung! It's not a laugh a minute but it is good fun. Robert's other trademark is the speech he uses in his games and BOTSB is 
no exception. It may look ropy and it may be a weird idea but it's good fun to play. Additionally, there are lumps of dung to hide under. No, we don't fully understand how Robert's head works either...

212386.overview: A basic, German language horizontally scrolling space shooter set after the events of the previous games. You have at least kill 40% of the enemies or destroy the meteors on the levels to finish the level. A pretty easy horizontally shoot em up. A lot of swervy alcoholic aliens, meteors, bonus and even a crazy story:  You’re a drunken alien-hunter who had lost your job and needed to do this to redeem yourself. Coded by using special Amal features.

212387.overview: An attractively outfitted Billiard table awaits for a nice game. Step in, light up a cigar and have a brandy while you set up your next shot. Enjoy having your servant set up the table for you and never any chalk on your nice suit.

212388.overview: A basic, German language horizontally scrolling space shooter set in the year 2294. You have at least kill 40% of the enemies or destroy the meteors on the levels to finish the level.

212399.overview: A first person RPG for the Amiga, originally the final entry in the Black Dawn series though it would eventually be followed by Black Dawn Rebirth in 2019.

212400.overview: A homebrew Sokoban variant style game created by Martin Button and released in 1996.

212402.overview: More of a four level demo than a full game, this platfomer was created by Dave and Den Software and released in 1997.

212403.overview: Released as part of Amiga Classix 3 Classic, game was packaged with a level creator. Created by Marcus 'Mops' Johansson with music by Goran Nilsson using Blitz BASIC, AMOS and Personal Paint, the full version of the game has intro, outro, high-score saving and jumps from 10 levels to 99.  Grab the gems, the keys and push the like colors together. The game will get more difficult as you go.

212404.overview: Published in Assassins 3 The Ultimate Games CD, this Breakout\Arkanoid bat and ball game was created in Blitz BASIC by JP Hamilton.

212405.overview: High-speed jet boat racing! Be fast off the line, make it through all the gates and back to the finish and leave the losers in your wake!

212412.overview: A strategic board game for up to 4 players, coded in Amos Pro by Volker Stepprath. Several different starting boards are available for use. The goal is to get the largest amount of dots changed to your team color. Jump and work around to leave balls. A strategic game for 1 up to 4 players, the aim is to leave balls after you turned so that other player couldn’t take a move anymore. But be careful cause there are pitfalls on board.

212413.overview: Probably best known as the precursor to the genuinely loved sequel Boron II, this game is difficult because you are dead with a single hit. Just as in real life you get one shot at it. It is a shooter, but offers some challenging navigation elements as well, plus a pretty intimidating boss. It is unfortunately the first and final boss rolled into one. It's a short game which can likely be played in less than 2 minutes by someone who knows the foes and challenges of it.

212414.overview: This game starts out looking like a straight-forward horizontally scrolling shooter, but the entire first wave you might as well not shoot your weapon, it is all about avoiding shots fired and oncoming meteors, but from then on becomes a full on shooter. Like the first game in the series you only have one life to give for your hobby. If you get hit you have to start from scratch. Unlike the original, you proceed past the first boss and are greeted by a mix of shooting and avoid-it areas throughout the alien complex to a second boss. If you can take him out, the game is complete. Though you might want to let it play on after completion as the music is pretty funky.

212415.overview: A Tetris game created with Blitz BASICby Leigh Bowers for Tyrrell Corp in 1995. You can set how many rounds in each section and start level. You can have it keep stats on your games and other standard settings. The game has different tile sets and you can choose whether to have sound effects, music or nothing.  The sounds effects may sound familiar.

212416.overview: A game of Black Jack written in AMOS BASIC 1.2 by Peter Craven, released in July 1991 and tested on the Amiga 2000 and Amiga 500. Choose between one and two players or play against the computer. Choose number of card desks to use to practice counting cards or make things extremely random.

212417.overview: 40 levels of puzzle action fun and 20 bonus levels, lots of music choices and more bonuses than the original\demo version. Created by Alistair Griffin of Vector 7 and released in 1997. Some colors you can slide over, some you can only cross once. Others you need to route around. Grab all the items and exit the level.

212418.overview: The original Block Buster game was an example game with the Easy AMOS development tool. This is a fan made "improvement" where the ball is significantly faster. Some might say, impossibly faster.

212419.overview: The demo for this game was released, but the full version was scheduled for release in 1998. According to German interviews with Michael Garlich of Titan, the game was cancelled because the "final version" submitted by the programmers was considered too buggy for commercial release [Sources: Amiga Future, Apr/May 99 issue; NoCover #53, June 98 issue.] and because of military, school and other commitments by the primary coders. Still this first person shooter in the shadow of Doom\Wolfenstein games was intriguing enough to have a lot of people willing to play the unfinished product.

212420.overview: An Arkanoid style game created by Lodge and released to PD in 1995.

212421.overview: A very simple breakout game with some updates to make it more attractive and interesting. It was created by Paul J. Champion and released to PD in 1994.

212422.overview: Move the available pipes and platforms around in order to move the ball towards the end of the level.

212423.overview: Briscola is one of Italy's most popular games, together with Scopa and Tressette. A little-changed descendant of Brusquembille, the ancestor of Briscan and Bezique, Briscola is a Mediterranean trick-taking, Ace-Ten card game for one against the computer, played with a standard Italian 40-card deck.

212424.overview: A motorcycle racing management game for Division One racing created by VGS Software and released in 1993. VGS Software released several versions, of this game with additional heats and another game for Division Two riders.

212425.overview: A Galaxian style space shooter written in AMOS by Zeljko Kolarevicis and released on Amiga Format cover disk 136B.

212426.overview: Another little arcade worm game with "hi scores" at stake that will guarantee you some wild games :-). The principle? You are a kind of worm, at the top of the screen, and undergo a vertical scrolling, namely that the screen moves from bottom to top, and that on the playing area, there are plenty of obstacles. On your side, you can only move to the left and to the right, the goal being to accumulate the greatest number of points possible (a bit like for Fnurr 2000 ) while avoiding as many obstacles as possible.

212427.overview: A Blitz BASIC shooter game created by Dave McGlashen using sprites from a couple of other games, but it runs smooth and is fun to play.

212689.overview: A sophisticated new Fruit Machine (slot machine) game setup from TDM. Gambling without the mess and smell of smoke and old cocktails. Multiple ways to enjoy the fun, nudge a any time if you have earned them. Beautiful Black Knight themed graphics. Originally Shareware but later converted to Public Domain by the authors.

212690.overview: The precursor to Blocks XL, a columns clone on the Amiga from Engine Nine Design coded by Matt Briggs. It involves arranging falling blocks in such a way as to clear them. They are groups of 3 same-size but varying color blocks, which must be arranged into sequences of 3 or more, either horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Sequences of 4 or 5 count for double or triple points, and diagonal sequences score the most. The real trick is to set up 'combos' - where one line causes other blocks to drop so as to create other lines.

212692.overview: The sequel or full version perhaps of Blocks by Engine Nine, a columns clone on the Amiga from Engine Nine Design coded by Matt Briggs. It involves arranging falling blocks in such a way as to clear them. They are groups of 3 same-size but varying color blocks, which must be arranged into sequences of 3 or more, either horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Sequences of 4 or 5 count for double or triple points, and diagonal sequences score the most. The real trick is to set up 'combos' - where one line causes other blocks to drop so as to create other lines.

212693.overview: Released as part of the Now That's What I Call Games 3 compilation, this game is a mix of American Football and a monster bloodfest. Teams can be created and traded with others. Bring your best team to fight your pal's!

212694.overview: Released on Assassins CD4 this strategy game for up to 4 players was created by Marko Turunen and released in 1995.

212695.overview: Move the image sections around to match the overall image shown. Match things exactly and move on to the next image!

212696.overview:
A little game made by the demoscene group Tristar sometime between 2012 and 2013.

Unfortunately there is only 4 levels and after that it says "Demo finished).

212697.overview: Welcome to the first version of Bomber GUG. We have tried to make an easy, smooth and wonderful game, based on the very popular Bomberman games. The game is not yet perfect and there may be some bugs in the bogs. See the docs for more info. Made in Blitz BASIC 2.1.

212698.overview: Based on the classic arcade style game from the very early 80's. You pilot a small airplane, and your mission is to bomb the city to oblivion, or at least flat enough where you can safely land.

212699.overview: A Spanish language artillery game, like Scorched Earth for 2 players by Pedro Gil aka Balrog. Released to public domain as a beta version in 1996.

212700.overview:
A game dedicated to all of the men and women, who's job is to protect and serve the public. Thank you...  
 
First choose your player and name him. Each of the 4 Bomb Squad members have different levels and ranks. You have pullers and cutter tools and must use your moves wisely to disable the explosive before the time runs out. Cut in the wrong place and you may detonate and destroy a building. Luckily you get to continue. Good luck, no booms!

213434.overview:
How hungry is Blockman? Blockman is SO hungry that if he can't find anything to eat, it might actually kill him! Eat and eat what you can, and if you eat
enough, then Blockman will happily launch himself into his next mealground.

213596.overview:
A Load Runner clone, "BloadRunner" has 20 levels, and in the "instructions" file on the disk it said "This game is NOT shareware. I will send a version out with more screens to anyone who sends me a small gift", so sounds like there could be one with more levels. Version 1.7, which had 38 level files on the disk. Level 35 is not complete so it lacks a spawn point for the player etc. Level 38 (last level) was just a short and easy maze. The game has no ending. The game appears to be a conversion from an Apple game. Like in the original, the evil empire has stolen a huge cache of gold from its rightful owners, and your mission is to infiltrate its treasury and recapture it. This entails progressing through up to 38 screens of platforms, ladders and ropes.

The Empire has sent robotic guards down to protect the gold, and contact with any of these will cost you a life. Your method of escaping them is to press fire to dig a hole in their line of movement, thus causing them to fall in briefly, allowing you to move across the gap safely. Once all the gold has been collected, a ladder allowing you to move onto the next screen is added. Completing these screens often requires forward planning and precision.

213597.overview: A game inspired by the 8-Bit Wizard series of platfomers that came out concurrent with Jumpman games. This game has you collecting the treasures, using the ladders, ropes and platforms to gather them all. Unlike the wizard games there are a limited amount of baddies per level who often travel in a set course around the screen, allowing you to anticipate and avoid them.

213598.overview: A 2D role playing game\arena fighting game that supported up to 4 simultaneous players it was eventually released in Amiga Future, June 2005, but prior versions by Scott Seiler of 2Xs had been on the net since 1998.

213659.overview: An earlier form of this game was being played thousands of ears ago. It has since evolved into an enthralling game, in which chance and tactics go hand in hand. The object of the game is to be the first one to get all your pieces home and to move them outside the board. Barriers are set up on the way and double bets serve to heighten the tension. Once  you are engrossed in the game, you will quickly discover why the game has survived all these centuries.

213660.overview: A scrolling screen platform for two players only, created by Ben Wyatt, released to PD in 1992. This was Ben Wayatt's first game creation.

213679.overview: A classic game of Battle Ship that you play against the computer. You can set the difficulty level from 1 where the computer isn't very bright to 9 where the computer is very hard to beat. The game features mouse control. This game features 5 ships to place. It was created by Bob Akerberg and released to PD in 1996.

213680.overview: Published by the Emerald Mine Club of Oz (Australia and New Zealand), this Emerald Mine variant was created by Team Lazarus and went by several names such as Beer Mines and Beer Mines I. The game includes the hungry yam yams and many levels of fun and is a very nice example of an Emerald Mine game from 1995.

213681.overview: A fairly straightforward Asteroids clone with pre-rendered graphics, created by Andrea Doimo and first sent off for the Amiga Format Blitz Basic Competition in 1995, but was never published by them. Now available on the author's Github.

213682.overview: A single player shooter, created using the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit for the Amiga. It seems to want to be a less claustrophobic Gauntlet style game. You shoot swords at troglodytes, ghosts and wizards, pick up potions, shoot bony spawn points, grab treasure and avoid pit traps.

213683.overview: Shoot blocks, which ricochet off the ice and can remove similar shapes. Once you have removed enough of the blocks you can move on to the next level. The right hand panel shows the stage, the remaining blocks until you move on and the time countdown. Released on the Astronut & Wise Man 4 pack, and in Issue 4 of the Amiga Power magazine in August 1991 on the included Amiga Power Disk 4.

213684.overview: Blob-A-Blob by AmigaLive in 1990, you play as a Green Blob, and your task is to colour up all the Tiles on each platform while avoiding the nasties that lurk around. Your only method of avoiding the Nasties is a Jump Up method, so timing is definitely key here, as jumping too early or late, will cause your life to be drained, as there is no on screen counter for this sadly, You kinda have to guess at your remaining life left. There are switches to press, which can reveal other tiles to change colour of, or indeed teleports (which look like a flat-V shape on each platform) will teleport you to another platform. There is some in-game Music what plays, if you are dead or not started the game, sound effects will play instead and enemies will just randomly move around until you Play. While this Game works in Kickstart 2+ as the Sludge Creatures will cover up the Tiles making them hard to see, so it is included in the KS1.3 Collection.

213685.overview: First title screen shows Blop Blox and second shows Blox Blox. This is a Tetris clone with some surprises including special effect that will cross the shaft that the shapes fall down and if they impact the shape it can delete or change them suddenly to new forms, When the game speeds up on later levels, this can really throw a wrench in the works!

213686.overview: A Dyna Blaster aka Bomberman clone for up to 4 users by Nick Gravgaard and released to PD in 1997.

213687.overview: Bomber Jack is a clone of Bomb Jack. The main character of the game is Jack. His task is to collect all the bombs on the board, avoiding movement paths of the numerous enemies such as shadow girls or flying objects and contact with red bombs. The only available weapon is short and long jumping ability combined with a perfect timing when trying to find a gap between the enemies plus possibility decelerating of falling.

213688.overview: A shareware platformer by Simon Gustavsson and Karl-Magnus Johansson, published in 1994. An cute platformer in which you clear baddies from each screen while collecting as many fruit as you can for bonus points. Baddies usually take several hits and speed up after the first one. Your standard boomerang can be upgraded to a fireball with a powerup found in some of the levels. There is also an umbrella that lets you skip two of a total of 100 levels. Coded in AMOS and using AMOS stock sounds.

213689.overview:
A solitaire card game where you group all the cards in sets of 13 cards in ascending sequence by suit from Ace to King.  This 52-card solitaire starts with the entire deck shuffled and dealt out in four rows. The aces are then moved to the left end of the layout, making 4 initial free spaces. You may move to a space only the card that matches the left neighbor in suit, and is one greater in rank. Kings are high, so no cards may be placed to their right (they create dead spaces).

When no moves can be made, cards still out of sequence are reshuffled and dealt face up after the ends of the partial sequences, leaving a card space after each sequence, so that each row looks like a partial sequence followed by a space, followed by enough cards to make a row of 14.

213690.overview: A Pac-Man clone starring a hungry lemon looking for dots to eat but don't let the baddies get you! If you work hard you can trap one of the ghosts in your spawn point and but while there are no power pills in this game there are special items that allow you to place wall blocks and make other interesting changes to play.

213691.overview: A one person, bounce the ball game. Use your joystick to keep the ball bouncing onto the boxes. Each box contains a point value and you get that if you can stop the ball on the box. If the ball stops bouncing click the fire button to shoot it upwards. There are bonuses to grab, nasty critters that will pop your ball and a unique control system.

213694.overview: A solitaire card game by the prolific Harald Müller (Mueller), released by both Intersoft and Schatztruhe in 1995.

213695.overview: Brainbow the rainbow puzzler by Aaron Fisher, released in 1992 and part of the Assassins game releases. Each level gives you 3 shapes to use. The goal is to make the whole screen the same color. You are given a certain number of shapes to use on the screen and must make all the changes in that amount of moves. Medium and Hard difficulty give you less shapes to use.

213696.overview: Considered a hidden gem of Amiga games, this was released on ASI-GAMES-VOL 144 and was created by Andrew Campbell. It has two variations of game: Gravity and Sliders. Brain Shave is the sequel to Enigma a PD game available on the Funhouse disk and on the Assassin's collection, in this new game. It is a game like White Rabbit or Enigma where the object of the game is to match up all the colored tiles by dragging them around the screen using a joystick controlled cursor. Select, press and hold fire and drag the file if it is free to move.

213715.overview:
Bubble Pop Memory is a freeware Memory-style game. 32 cards are placed face down in a random order on the screen, and the goal is to locate the 16 pairs of identical cards in the least possible amount of trials. The player can click on two cards at once to reveal their value. If they are identical, they remain visible. If they are different, they are flipped down again. The player has 4 minutes to complete the game.

The best scores are recorded in a high score table.

213716.overview:
Bubblestones is a game by Guy Maysonnave, several versions were released with the most common being BubbleStones v1.4 and BubbleStones v2.0. They are the same game with only minor modifications. The goal of BubbleStones is to clear all the Bubbles from 25 different levels before they touch your base. When you connect 3 stones of the same color, they disappear and in doing so they remove any stones that were connected below them. At the beginning of each level you start with 1999 points and the countdown starts. A destroyed stone brings back 10 points, a stone which falls 50 points, a bonus clock gives 200 points. All these are added to the meter and at the end of the level what is there will be added to your score or withdrawn if the number is in the negatives.  
 
You can continue past the 25th level at a faster pace.

213717.overview: Released on the red floppy coverdisk from Amiga Computing, this single player shooter by Morgan Henry has an upgrade path to improve parts of your "ship" and choose shot type.

213718.overview: An AMIGA tribute to the Bust A move Games this game was written using blit basic on an amiga 1200 by my brother and I in 1997. It was given a good review by Amiga Format and CU Amiga magazine. Three player enhanced and one player modes.

213719.overview: In English the rough translation is find matches or find couples. It is a version of the well-known Memory game. You can select between different letters and sizes. The voice synthesizer reproduces the names of the countries to which the flags belong, in case you use this option. It is programmed in AMOS.

213833.overview:
BoulderDäsh is a clone of the original Boulder Dash on C64.
It has seen many development updates since 1987.

Features:
• 1:1 BoulderDäsh clone
• Full speed under MC68000 Amigas with AGA, ECS or OCS
• Full graphic board support! Up to 256 Colors (depends on graphic set)
• Full sound card support (AHI)!
• System friendly! Can be paused and resumed at any time.
• requires OS 2.04 or higher
• Commodore styleguide conform
• Locale 
• Great GUI
• Online Help
• many preferences windows
• Up to six players
• New game elements
• Unique record and play feature to show others how you solved the caves.
• Internal music player with playlist
• Optional full screen mode when running in RTG mode.
• 10000 Levels
• 36 graphic sets
• 6 character sets
• 5 sample sets
• Several hiscorelists for each game (game, level and level time records)
• Level and game editor
• Supports C64 and Atari Construction Kit Level and game files.
• Levels up to 100 * 100 blocks
• Special gravitation modes
• Create your personal game graphics
• Create your personal sample sets
• Create your personal game music

213842.overview: Bouncer is a Breakout-style reaction game released in 1987 by Diamond.

213908.overview:
A one or two player card game using Tarot cards. Each pack of cards has 40 cards, 10 for each suit, the suits are Gold (coins), Cups, Clubs and Spades (swords) and are numbered 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11 and 12 (there are no 8's or 9's). Only 1,3,10, 11 and 12 are worth points (Briscas). 1=11 points, 3=10 points, 10=2 points, 11=3 points and 12=4 points. There are 120 points total available, if each player gets 60 it will be a tie. After dealing one card is dealt face up and this card represents LIFE and the rest of the un-dealt cards are face down next to LIFE. At each turn, a card is played and the other player tries to KILL that card. The one that kills keeps the pair. Players keep 3 cards in their hand, drawing to keep that level.  
 
LIFE kills all cards except another LIFE of a higher value. 3 of LIFE kills a 12 of LIFE, but a 12 of LIFE kills any other suit. You can kill a card with a higher number of the same suit. Modem play was available.

214239.overview: Did you enjoy Megaball 2.1 and 3.0, how about Megaball 4.0 for AGA? Well how about the game that started it all for the Mackey brothers, the Ball before it was Mega! This Arkanoid-style Block Breaker Game lets you play the original incarnation.

214782.overview: A casino style card game created by Dan Cogilano and released in 1990. It features info on game strategy, allows practice and house rules.

214785.overview:
At last. . . . . a bridge player that gives you a challenging game with a really tough opponent. We can promise you hours of enjoyment as you pit your wits against this powerful program.

And now a superb new feature for the beginner and improver . . . . a special tutorial section devised by an expert to guide you through the intricacies of bidding and play with twenty set hands and detailed explanation.

This is a bridge player for both the expert and the beginner, with versatile bidding routines that really set a high standard, matched by the emphatically powerful play of the cards. The computer will play as either defender or declarer. Generates random hands and allows proper bidding in the Acol system, including the Stayman and Blackwood conventions.

Bid against the computer, then prove your skill as it takes you on playing both your opponents hands.

Make use of the many superb features - including one or to that can give you the edge against the machine!

OPTIONS INCLUDE. . . . .

    Tutorial section with 20 set hands, advice and explanation.
    Improve your game - Post mortem facility allows you to rebid and replay and hand.
    Review bidding or play to previous tricks while playing a hand.
    Input a contract of your own choice to test yourself.
    Peep at your opponents hands.
    Comprehensive on-screen information displays - contract, tricks won so far, cards played in current and last trick, score.
    Option to bias the deal to give you and your 'partner' more high card points if you prefer to play as declarer.
    At any time claim the rest of the tricks.
    Restart the play of the cards.

214786.overview: Bridge Player Galactica is a Bridge card game with betting elements, developed and published by Oxford Softworks, which was released in Europe in 1989. Game written in HiSoft BASIC. Original coding by Richard Wheen and Nicola Gardener; Amiga conversion by Ian Stirzaker and Chris Whittington.

214787.overview:
Bobo Kloc is a timed arcade puzzle-board game from Jan Guzik and Ewelina Żyradzka with two gameplay modes. Accessing the next stage requires removing or gathering all of the tiles and objects placed on the board. There are ten types of tiles, removal requires a collision with another block of the same type. The task is complicated by numerous bugs (contact with them means a loss of life), objects (box, bulb, wall, rock) and types of surfaces (ice, rocks, swamp). The bugs are divided into intelligent, lethargic and nervous, differing in the speed and the way of movement. The game features also some power up items, such us snowflake (temporarily freeze enemies), bomb (kills one wave of enemies), hearth (extra life), clock (extra time), level pass (next level), floppy disk (extra points), teleport (gate to another part of the board) and in game hints.

In Bobo mode Amigafly can change the direction of movement after hitting an obstacle (wall, box, object, end of the board) or reaching special blocking surface (swamp). This type of game requires quick planning and predicting the path of movement while avoiding numerous enemies on board. By contrast, there are no restrictions in movement in the Kloc mode.

Bobo mode features 110 levels, Kloc mode 50. After each completed level the player receives an access password. The game was originally created for the polish side of LK Avalon but was not published at the time. 

The game has built-in level editor, allowing to add an own set of the boards.

214788.overview: An Amiga bridge playing program. You play with a computer partner against two computer opponents. It includes an online Bridge tutorial. A hint mode is available in all situations.

214849.overview: Bedroom Olympiad is an Adult orientated Action game, developed by Shockwave, which was released in 1988.

214853.overview:
The BIG ONE Lotto Systems generator & manager is a must for anyone who plays Lotto.
This is a professional Lotto systems research tool that gives you greater control over your Lotto investment.

Features include:
• Generates Systems Lotto games.
• Generates unique minimum overlap systems.
• Create a $300 system that assures a win.
• Run your own syndicate size systems.
• Make your own quick path system.
• Enter your own systems for analysis.
• Stores all systems to a data disk.
• Checks any systems accurately against draws.
• Lotto Draw Archive included and maintained.
• Statistical analysis of any systems.
• Output to screen or printer.

214854.overview: Birds N' Bees is a sex education game, published by IntraCorp, which was released in 1988.

214861.overview: An Emerald Mine style Boulderdash game created by De Bond and released commercially in 1993 with over 80 levels of difficult play.

214863.overview: This fan game created by Lazer or Laser (depending on which title screen you believe) of No One inc. It has a setup screen like Emerald Mine. The usual rules apply except that the falling diamonds don't crush the butterflies, although they can crush you.

214888.overview:
After the Infamous events at Base DS97 Brenn barely escaped with his life. The Horrors of the Black Dawn left behind him in the burnt crater of that desolate, haunted moon.

Or so he thought……

Slowly, the horrors infiltrated Brenn`s mind, through dreams twisting the thoughts, morals and his very soul. The Black Dawn lived on driving the once proud hero into the one thing he thought so hard to defeat.

Driven mad and paranoid, fearful of the demons he fought, Brenn built a fortress to protect himself and populated the fortress with robot protectors to keep the world, and the Demons at bay, The loneliness and Isolation got worse as the fortress expanded taking over the small moon that it was based upon wiping out the local population until only he remained. You have been hired to enact revenge for the relatives of the fallen.

214919.overview:
Development started 17 February 1997. The aim was to create a 1 or 2 player game in the style of Chaos Engine. During the development, the game became more and more like the old Brutal Homicide (a 2-player versus game).

Sadly, the game never got really stable and development stopped. This beta version was the only release made.

214971.overview: A sliding piece puzzle game created by Simon Dye for Digital Obsession. A level editor could be obtained by sending 50p to the author. Bulldozer Bob extends the basic sliding puzzle game formula by giving you the ability to flip a block from the front of your player sprite to the back, from the left to the right, and vice versa. Each level must be completed within an allowed number of moves. (It is either this or a timer in these games.) In most levels, there are also special tiles that allow movement in only one direction or tiles that break after you moved over them.

215005.overview: Dawn - A New Beginning Remix is just the slightly changed full Shareware version of Dawn - A New Beginning. It is now available as freeware. PD-Soft listed this game as No. 4125. It is a 2D role playing\dungeon crawler game released in 1996 by ZSoft.

215103.overview: Boris Ball is a Breakout variant. The player controls a paddle at the bottom of the screen which can move left and right. A ball bounces between the paddle and blocks which are placed towards the top of the screen. The goal is to remove all destructible blocks by hitting them with the ball. If the ball falls out of the bottom of the screen, a life is lost. Destroying blocks may cause a power-up to fall down which has positive or negative effects when picked up, e.g. a longer paddle, shooting out balls straight from the paddle, reversed controls or a level-skip. There are overall 100 levels and it comes with a handy level editor.

215147.overview: Belote (French pronunciation: ​[bəlɔt]) is a 32-card, trick-taking, Ace-Ten game played primarily in France, where it is one of the most popular card games both casually and in gambling.  Within the game's terminology, Belote is used to designate a pair of a King and a Queen of a trump suit, possibly yielding the game's name itself. Game by Jean-Stéphane Martin it was to be published by E.S.A.T. Software but closed shop only a few days before the game was supposed to be released.

215148.overview: This single player puzzle game was created by Digital Perceptions and relesed in 1994 in two forms, a PD demo version or a commercial full version. In it you must recreate the pattern given by shifting columns and rows. It starts out relatively easily allowing you to understand how it works and then gets progressively harder with each new level.

215149.overview: Push stones around a complex maze in this puzzle game by D. Cole that was released in 1990.

215372.overview: A Carvus style, platform game, the full version has 30 levels, the demo has only 3. Birdie woke up one day to find all his pals on the beach had been turned into grey, sad blocks. Your mission is to run over the blocks and bring their color back. The baddies must be avoided and bubbles can be burst for extra points. Keep your eyes open for extra lives which may float amongst the bubbles. The screen wraps around vertically so use this to your advantage. Passwords for the current level are shown on the score bar.

215378.overview:
The system includes a board (snowboard or surfboard) that connects to the joyport and 3 games: BIFF BOARDIN, URBAN SURFIN, & BIFF SELECT. Originally intended to be released on the Amiga CD32 and the Amiga line. It is unclear if this was an unreleased prototype or just had a very limited local North American commercial release.

The game was released on the CD32, however the standard Amiga version got cancelled.

215477.overview: The Big 100 is a compilation of over 100 PD games for multiple systems, featuring a different set for each system. The vast majority of the included games are board game translations, e.g. backgammon, chess or checkers. The rest features various genres, but mostly falling block puzzles and variants of arcade games.

215500.overview: You must shoot the Alien in the head as many times as possible until its eventual demise and you've won. The game is played in a third person in the style of Quake or Doom. Indeed some graphics from Quake are present in the current build brought to us by mastaszek in 2019, first alphas released in 2017.

215528.overview: This is Keith Bugeja's unfinished Sonic clone "Blaze", two playable levels.

217260.overview:
Blower is a local multiplayer game, a Bomberman x Doom game. Let's say a Doom like with 2D bomberman fashion, or a Bomberman without bombs but with guns and flamethrower.
This version is a port to Amiga created for the Amiga Blitz Basic Game Jam.

217290.overview:
A four-player, Bomberman style game created with AMOS and created by Mantasoft Blast Squad, which started off life named Bomber Blaster, is a Bomberman clone which features all the elements you might reasonably expect in a game of this ilk, which includes Dyna Blaster and Blitz Bombers.

The one and two player campaign mode allows those without additional players close by to work through the game (the version on this site also features a level selector cheat if you want to see it all!).

If four players are on hand the battle mode increases the fun tenfold. The multiplayer is really the best way to experience Bomberman clones and this game is no exception.

The control options support a four-player adapter so no-one need go without a joystick. In addition there is an option for a CD32 pad.

Visually the game is varied but check out Aristides' unused artwork on the Extras page to see where the look of the graphics may have headed. They show a stronger Japanese style which is appropriate given the origins of Bomberman. Unlike most other similar games Blast Squad supports graphics cards which shows how Andrew was aiming to support a wide range of Amigas.

217536.overview: Boxx is a small platform game that was originally made in 2014 for the Commodore Amiga. But it was made with Backbone so it had poor performance. Now, in 2022, the game is ported to the much better Scorpion Engine and runs a lot smoother.

219266.overview: Bertie's Animal Kingdom is an Animal recognition game designed for nursery and pre-school children. The only requirement is that the child must have a basic knowledge of how to use a mouse Keyboard controls are not required except to enter the child's name for the hi-score table. All actions which the child does highlight different areas of the screen in a bright color so that they know what they are doing if they click the mouse button on that spot.

219361.overview: A bodged together, homebrew pastiche of Mortal Kombat and other popular martial arts fighting games created by the aptly named Sarcastic Gits.

278859.overview: A remake of the classic Game & Watch multi-screen game Lifeboat for your Amiga computer, created by Mike Verstaevel and released in 1999.  In the game, you'll have to maneuver two lifeboats and catch people who are jumping out of a ship on fire.

417679.overview: Once upon a time, in a distant land, there lived a little box-like creature named Cubo. Cubo was a happy-go-lucky creature who loved nothing more than exploring his world and find new areas.

418076.overview: No One is a legend for Boulder Dash heads and this is considered one of the best Boulder Dash games for the Amiga. It underwent multiple versions over the years but contains levels converted from the C64 games from multiple Boulderdash games including Boulderdash, Boulderdash 2-4 and the Boulderdash Construction Kit. The setup screen might lead you to believe it supported the usual 2 players, in fact it only supports a single player.

418309.overview: A PD vertically scrolling space shooter created by Mirage Holland in 1989.

418310.overview: A multi-choice text adventure where you play a police officer and must try to stay alive and keep down the civilian body count while making it through a day on the streets.

418312.overview: A PD/Freeware Boulder Dash or Emerald Mine clone created by Monty Bob and released in 1991. It has a teamwork mode where two players can work together to clear the level.

418317.overview: A text adventure created by The Dual Crew and released as PD Freeware in 1990 where you play as a roided-up,  super aggressive police officer.

418374.overview: A single-player, homebrew vertically scrolling shooter created by Fez Software using the  Shoot-'Em-Up-Construction Kit (SEUCK). Called a Cute'em-up this game also had a sequel: Pee Bee: Revenge is Cute.

418388.overview: A shareware horizontally scrolling military air shooter created by Paul Young.  Blast all manner of enemy airships out of the skies. You'll have to take down everything from zeppelins and bi-planes to the latest in advanced fighters jets and attack helicopters.

418429.overview: A multi-scrolling shooter created by Three Little Elks and released to PD\Freeware in 1995. Bratwurst is the same kind of game as Gravity Force and Roketz. The difference is that it uses vector graphics instead of ordinary bitmap graphics. This  enables the map and players to be scaled easily which means that when the players are close to each other the camera will zoom in on the players to get a more detailed view. Another difference with Bratwurst is that four players can play simultaneously.

418433.overview:
An open source conversion of the old DOS game to the Amiga in 2017. To exit the level, the player must ollect a bomb on every map and bring it to a security cube; the bomb will destroy the cube allowing the player to use the exit.

It features 24 new levels, played in a single episode in a linear fashion (despite a between level map trying to convince you otherwise), a new weapon, the Plasma Discharger (which functions as the game's ultimate weapon), and several new bad guys and bosses.

Though the "new bad guys" comment is a little misleading as only one of them is actually all new; the others are the boss aliens from Aliens of Gold (with their stats reduced to non-boss level) or simply slightly edited and re-coloured bad guys from the previous game.

418620.overview: BINARY is a puzzle game in which you remove\consume stones in 3000 possible configurations, which are always in pairs There is always a solution, but is it the nicest one? An options menu and the help query complete the game. Released in both Amiga Fun and on 1993-04-08 on Amigo! issue 02/93.

418686.overview:
An open source conversion of the 90's DOS game for the Amiga. Work done by  Monolith Productions, and Szilard Biro. Like in the original, you play as Caleb. Caleb was once a feared gunslinger, until he met a woman who was involved with a mysterious cult known as Cabal. Caleb, too, is sucked in, and soon becomes one of the Chosen - the most favored worshipers of the evil god Tchernobog. But one day, Tchernobog inexplicably kills the four Chosen, including Caleb. Mysteriously resurrected years later, Caleb is out to get revenge, and learn why his lord cast him down so abruptly.

Blood is a first-person shooter with horror elements, which uses the Build engine. Similarly to Duke Nukem 3D, the environment is interactive: many objects can be physically moved or affected in other ways. Destruction of landscapes is possible (although only in specific spots), with bullet holes being left by misplaced shots. The Build engine version is 2.5D, so there are rooms above rooms and puzzles which are based on this.

The game consists of four episodes, each containing a set of maps that have to be traversed by the protagonist in a specific order. The levels are usually realistic-looking structures, e.g. a carnival complete with twisted attractions, a city district, a moving train, etc.

Throughout the levels, Caleb will have to find keys (up to six in a level) and hit switches in order to work his way to the exit. On the way, he will meet a variety of enemies, such as zombies that tend to come back to life after killed, cultists armed with shotguns and tommy-guns that shout in pseudo-Latin language, crawling hands that attempt to choke him, hell-hounds that can set him on fire with their breath, and many more. Boss battles await Caleb at the end of each episode.

To defend himself against this menace, Caleb utilizes a variety of weapons: a pitchfork; a flare gun that can set enemies on fire; a sawed-off shotgun; a tommy-gun; a napalm launcher; TNT bundles which come in three different varieties; a home-made flamethrower made of an aerosol can; a tesla cannon that electrocutes enemies; a magical staff dubbed "Life Leech"; and a voodoo doll.

There are items to pick up strewn around. Unlike most other 3D shooters, the protagonist's health is not replenished via medikits, but by "Life Essences", heart-like power-ups randomly dropped by enemies upon their death. It is also possible to find armor, which comes in three different varieties - Physical, Fire, and Spiritual, each one defending Caleb from different attacks. There are also other power-ups: some (such as Jumping Shoes or Doctor's Bag) can be picked up and activated at any time, while others (such as Partial Invisibility) activate immediately when taken.

As the title implies, violent and gory imagery plays a significant role in the game.

418937.overview: A one to four player wall-street strategy game created by Andreas Page and released as shareware in 1987. A very good German stock market game for up to 4 stock market speculators.

419543.overview: A Command & Conquer\Warcraft 2 style top down strategy game created by Ravager's Reality and released originally as shareware in 1996. It supports both single player and multiplayer games.  It also appeared on Amiga Format CD14. In addition, it had an associated map editor for creating your own scenarios.

419756.overview:
"Early on Sunday morning, June 22, the German flood poured across the frontier, in three great parallel surges between the Baltic Sea and the Carpatian Mountains." As the commander of a front line regiment, you will be part of that surge, aiming your tanks and infantry for the heart of Russia. Or, backed by your T-34s and massed artillery, you can be part of the rock that tide would eventually wash up against at Stalingrad.  

BATTLE TANK: BARBAROSSA TO STALINGRAD is a command oriented, viewpoint style study of the first half of the Second World War in the East. Your main maneuver elements are companies and platoons. The full range of TOES of the period are under your command, from recon vehicles to Panzer regiments. 7 pre-built scenarios allow the players to get immediately into the game, but the heart of the simulation is a build- your-own routine that allows you to create scenarios simulating innumerable actions between German and Soviet forces. 2 may play, or the computer will play either side. Design and development by S. Newberg & S. St. John; art by J. Kula.

420533.overview: Bulbmaster is a sokoban-style game with a twist. The player assumes the role of a mechanic whose task is to move electric spheres to their sockets. The challenge lies in the fact that wooden crates can only be moved one space at a time, whereas the electric spheres will roll until they encounter an obstacle!

420732.overview: A single player platform shooter created by Digital Realms Software and released as shareware  in 1993.

420740.overview: An overhead view shooter where you make your way through a space station, where you must fight against the automated defenses.

420813.overview:
A playable action demo created by Mike Carter, Dean and Ola. Far away in a land where Lego is made, a crisis was happening. The machines creating the Lego men were goofing up more than normal. All the reject Lego men had no legs so they had to wobble to move about. Two of these rejects weren't having any more of this and so wobbled to the creators hill in Lego land. Dr. Technic (the creator of Lego) knew what they were here to see him about and so before they could say too much offered them a challenge. 

"My mazes are becoming cluttered with loose bricks and are making them very untidy and difficult to wonder round. If you on your own or with a friend can clear them as best you can I will award you with a very special gift. I have one pair of legs left to which I will color and give to the winner. If you fail to get through the mazes then you will be killed. It won't be easy, oh no! I've created a gang of ghosts to wonder the lonely mazes in search of someone to scare...if they find you you'll know!"
