420828.overview: An action puzzle demo written with AMOSPro 2.0 brought to you by Larry McGahey in 1996.

420829.overview: A great remake of the 8 Bit classic game.  Move the buggy along shooting at the enemies.  Simple but great fun.  Tested on Amiga 500 with 1 meg expansion and kickstart 1.3.

420858.overview: An unreleased two player pong game by Ben Darling and Matt Gorle in 1997.

420862.overview: Your Jeet Kune Do is unstoppable but can you guide the little dragon to victory in this homebrew platformer written in ASM 68k and released like water over the rocks in the year 2000.

420865.overview: A four player bomberman style shareware game from Silicon Sircus, created in 1996.

420872.overview:
A “dark adventure” and a kind of “over-time” game. A game that develops over time. The actions of NPCs and those of the player are based on a lot of chance and mix with many different attributes of the characters involved. This creates a small sandbox world that you can design yourself. You have to respond to the characters' needs and observe their actions.

The player is unspokenly made governor of the place and is supposed to rebuild the destroyed “Little Meadow Grove” on behalf of his mistress. He has to decide about all the resources and fate of the place. But what lies behind the faces and in the darkness is not obvious. It is impossible to tell whether a farmer is a friend or an enemy.

420965.overview: A shooter preview from T. Antoniades, released in 1992. The eventual game was intended on being ultra-violent and gory but this crosshairs shooter is just a tepid warm up. Shoot the red targets and let the white ones stand.

420969.overview: BODERUNNER is a game using simple rules : You must run to collect treasures to get out the level. You can climb on rope and ladder and fall into holes. Enemies are running behind you, and the only weapon you get, is a magic powder than can make a block melt. This game is based on the old and so great LodeRunner.

421102.overview: Boxx 3 Remake is a platform game for Commodore Amiga. The original game from 2017 is now now remade with Scorpion Engine and has upgraded graphics.

421223.overview:
The Big End was a neat Super Skidmarks-style F1 racer due for the Commodore Amiga + CD32 in 1995. Sadly cancelled due to the dying market. Rather than just being a top-down racer, as was quite common at the time, The Big End would tilt things slightly to give a more 3D viewpoint of the action – similar to Super Skidmarks. The aim was to “create an accurate Formula One-style game, but in an accessible arcade style”, according to developer Craig Howard. 
 
Cars would handle realistically, and the 16 F1 tracks would be faithful to the originals, right down to the track times. There would be different weather types in various races to affect how the cars would handle. Then, between races you would also be able to configure your car and make improvements with a basic player/manager feature.

421224.overview: A one or two player platform shooter by Aszu, that took 9th place entry at the Retro Komp Gamedev Compo 2016. The game is still a work in progress, but the demo is playable.

421238.overview:
An unreleased prototype for a copter themed action game based on the movie of the same name. Game created by Earok in 2018 and that is simply a Time Events type game, in which we are presented with the final scene of the movie Blu Thunder (Blue Thunder in Spain) and we will have to press the arrow or shot keys at the moment opportune to advance through the film until reaching the end.  In the style of the famous game Dragon's Lair.  
 
This was done mainly as an engine prototype for an FMV game (Dragon's Lair style), no further work is intended. The engine went on to be used as the basis for the unofficial Amiga ports of TimeGal and Road Avenger.

421270.overview: BOFH: Servers Under Siege. Take the role  of BOFH as you arrive late at work to find your workplace is overrun by a group of insane activists.

421464.overview: An AMOS based shareware platform game with puzzle elements by Asa Margetts. You've been turned into a frog but must save your pet, Joe Bug. Make your way through the witch's castle to reunite with your trusty companion and maybe you'll also find a way to get back to being a human being!

421465.overview: An oddball single-level platform game where your goal is to kill the animals and find the crown or trophy.

421466.overview: Released on Assassins Disk 137(aka ASI-GAMES-VOL 137) with Escapade and Squigs, this is a 3 player Tron\Lightcycle style game created by Paul Linsell.

421467.overview: A single player S.E.U.C.K. shooter by Robert Sedler where you pilot a a biplane fighting its way behind enemy lines. Avoid the anti-aircraft fire, enemy aces and everything the enemy throws at you and survive to rule the skies.

421468.overview: Take on the role of the Swedish boy who one day decides to discover the world outside his room. He gets together his most important parts of gear and leaves out into the dangerous reality. Attention! This game should not be used by sensitive persons such as children and Christer Rindeblad.

421469.overview: A S.E.U.C.K. game in which you play a cute fire breathing dragon. The game was developed by Chris Clarke and released into the public domain in 1989.

421471.overview: Dexion's first shareware release, done on  July 25 1991. Game coding and GFX by Tox. Intro GFX by Natrix and Tox. Blue Boon is a 2 player game dogfight game. Both players are controlled by joystick for this fight to the death. Gadgets of both Power and Bean type can be found to repair or upgrade ships, depending on what you need.

421472.overview: A set of boulder dash levels created by Boulerwilli originally for the C64, converted to the Amiga by Posocopi Waldkirch in 1991 using the Emerald Mine engine but with added enemies and some nice title music.

421473.overview: Own your own burger joint, design and cook burgers and manage the shop. A freeware AMOS game from Stewart Howgarth from 1995.

421474.overview: Breaker!!! is a public domain Breakout/Arkanoid clone for the Amiga. It was developed by Niels Provos and released in 1990.

421476.overview: A simple bubble popping game from Tony Philipsson released as a coverdisk on the 1992 Jumpdisk magazine. Shoot the various balloons that fly across the screen, making sure they don't hit you!

421482.overview: A graphical management game based on the text games of old, with the majority of the game being created statistically rather than through gameplay, showing the outcome of goal\penalty kicks as you work your way through you season. You play as the owner\manager with rights to transfer, change the squad, view the finances, make changes to the stadium and work player trades to improve your outcome and income!

421485.overview: Bullseye is a video game that deals with sentimental conquests. Play with your criteria, and find the love of your life.

421552.overview: A horizontal shooter where you battle space eggs from MK-Soft in 1993.

421885.overview: Box is a shareware interactive adventure novel in which you guide the main character, making his decisions and interacting with the world about him. Interaction is achieved through an advanced text-only interface which can understand plain(ish) English sentences entered by the user.

421944.overview: Boxx 2 Remake is a platform game with shooter elements for Commodore Amiga. The original game from 2015 is now remade with Scorpion Engine and has upgraded graphics.

422489.overview: A commercial action game based on Flappy Bird written by Sami Vehmaa and released in 2023.

422664.overview: Bambinours: Formes et Couleurs is a single player edutainment video game for Amiga OCS, published in 1989 by Carraz Editions. A very simple game for little children of three to eight years of age. Its purpose is to teach a child to recognize shapes and colors: there is a double entry grid on the screen, with columns designated by different colors, and rows designated by different shapes. The task is to place pictures of objects of a certain shape and color that appear one by one on the right side of the screen to a corresponding place within the grid. The settings let you choose between five languages, as well as between 12 grid types and 14 object types.

422735.overview: Beastie Workers 0.4 is a puzzle game created by Andrey Martinenko, written in C++ / SDL and released under a GPL2 license in 2007. Help the daemon do his work!

422767.overview: Called the demo for what would be the greatest jump'n-shootie ever made, this game from Deadsoft was released in 1996.

422855.overview: A freeware AMOS karate simulator game where you practice your martial arts moves.

422856.overview: A four player dominoes game created by Black Lightning Software in 1997.

422857.overview: A freeware muscleman button-mashing game from Jean-Pierre Software and made in 1995. Mash the fastest and get a higher score.

422861.overview: A homebrew minesweeper style game from Close To The Edge in 1992.

422863.overview: A Czech language,freeware AMOS text adventure from Mistic Joe in 2008. Your quest is to get to the magical land of Beerland, where beer is bountiful and free.

422894.overview: Boomfield is a Minesweeper style puzzle game created by Alon Fliess and released as shareware in 1993. It has new features not found in contemporary versions of Minesweeper and supports Hebrew and English play and some great music.

423072.overview:
A world of claustrophobic, mysterious, puzzle-riddled, dangerous mazes where, surrounded by countless enemies, you hunt the Evil Masters down with the purpose of eliminating them and the pain they brought. Determination, concentration and quick reflexes will be your only allies in your desperate mission.

BOH is a retro-styled top-down shooter/dungeon crawler, influenced by many of the all-time classics of the two genres. You need to solve puzzles, collect items, open passages, avoid traps, kill the Evil Masters and their minions and ultimately come out of the mazes in one piece.

After ten years and 18 free updates, a new edition called "BOH Advance" was released. It was not a remake but simply the base game bundled with all the updates released so far.

423084.overview: 10 pin bowling scores archive system created by Mark Ward of Wacky Carrot Software in 1990. Create league tables, add players and teams update the info and manage your bowling teams and team competitions and championships. Create next year's handicaps and all the things your alley will need to bowl a strike for all your patrons.

423086.overview: A Czech language high school dropout text adventure game by Amiga Bestware Company in 1993.

423089.overview:
An Amiga freeware implementation by Titbit of Richard Dawkins' evolution game.  In this applet one can simulate evolution of bugs in which you play the role of natural selection. This is an idea described in Richard Dawkins' book `The blind watch maker'. Each frame of the applet contains the picture of some critterlike object. It is grown by a fixed set of instructions together with some input parameters which may vary. As the parameters change the picture changes. So we can view the parameters as a genotype of the critter, while the picture represents the phenotype.

By pushing a zap-button, six arbitrary parameter sets are generated and the corresponding pictures drawn. The select-button leaves the critter concerned fixed, while small random variations in its parameters are applied to grow the critters in the other frames. By expressing a preference for big critters, or small ones, or colorful ones, or any preference one might have, you can indeed shape the critter according to this preference. However, it will usually turn out that new surprising life forms show up whose traits are far more striking than what one originally intended.

423117.overview: An AMOS based homebrew game from Zcumbag and Bombjack, created in 1994. It is a bloody crosshairs shooter where people and pets walk across the screen in a straight line and you can blast them.

423123.overview: A German language, homebrew strategy game created by Karsten Schenk in 2000.

423181.overview:
The Balrog And The Cat is a humorous text adventure originally made for ZX Spectrum back in 1988. It was later converted to many platforms; Amiga finally got the conversion in 2019. 

This game sees the player take the role of Balrog, who's at home enjoying a green cheese sandwich, brown bread of course, when there's a scratching at his door. The source of the annoyance turns out to be a cat who got accidentally teleported there by a Wizard. The object of the game is to help the cat.

Along the way the player will encounter at least one troll, characters from other games and frequent pubs.

423184.overview:
BattleMech, sometimes confused with another Amiga game BattleTech for the simple reason the game itself occasionally confuses the names, is a mecha strategy game that can be played up to eight players. The aim is simply to kill other players before they kill you.

You first choose the mecha of your liking and then continue place it to the grid.  On each turn every player must choose a series of commands to perform at the end of the turn that will be launched simultaneously, including moving to a certain direction, jumping and attacking with a variety of weapons. The trick is to estimate what the other players will do succesfully; otherwise you'll be walking straight to their attacks while your own will hit air.

The game also features a "mecha factory" where you can create your own BattleMechs.

423324.overview:
Brutal Speed was a racing game planned for the AGA Amiga, briefly previewed in Italian Games Machine magazine issue 65 under the name of Speed Mania. It was also known as Speed ManiaX and eventually evolved into Brutal Speed. It was an impressive title that had 8 directional scroll at 1/4 pixels and 128 colours in total. It was similar in many ways to Super Cars 2, Overdrive and the likes of Neo Drift on the Neo Geo.

Although progressing very well and looking brilliant, it was just too late and along with several other games, it was cancelled. Previously the team had released another game which hardly sold at all, and just got pirated and spread everywhere. They decided to move onto other platforms instead, where they still go today over at https://www.xteamsoftware.com/

Sadly the developer confirmed they had lost pretty much everything when their A4000 HD had broke down. They have suggested that there might be backups, so something in the future could be recovered perhaps.

A playable demo was however released many moons ago when the game was known as Speed ManiaX, so you can at least check that out and see the promise of the title for yourself. Hopefully in the future we will get to learn more about the project and perhaps even find something more of the final game at the point of its cancellation.

423606.overview:
The story takes us to the Tian Shan mountain ranges, in the extreme northwest of China.

Legend has it that inside a lost valley, protected behind difficult-to-access gorges, a pagoda is hidden behind hectares of endless bamboo forests, sculpted by an order of ancient Buddhist warrior-monks. Fearful after the events that occurred during the Chinese Cultural Revolution, with the conquest of Tibet by the Maoists, the warrior monks have decided to resist. To do this, they have accepted the help of Lord X, a former criminal from Vietnam, wanted by the Hague Tribunal for the use of chemical weapons. He soon resumes his fateful experiments. Soon myriads of zombies begin to appear around the place, while the locals quickly flee to the hills. War of war,

Only you can stop it. As an expert martial arts fighter versed in Jit Kun Do, you have to face endless hordes of enemies that will crowd on both sides of the screen, barely being able to contain them.

Use your kicking and jumping skills to eradicate the overflowing zombie plague, dodge shurikens, and subject Lord to your redeeming justice.

423643.overview: An Arkanoid style freeware game from Paul Stevens in 1989. 10 different special drop bricks may show up to help or hinder you from clearing the bricks. Special score bonuses and lots of twists and turns.

423660.overview: A shareware text adventure game created by Mark Reynolds and released in 1993. Gather parts and make machines to battle your enemies!

423674.overview: A customizable implementation of minesweeper by R. Trueman, released as freeware in 1992. Choose the size of the playing field, the amount of bombs, the number of start squares and the level of overall difficulty.

423710.overview: Bizzy Bros is one of Loriciel's planned releases that were cancelled for no apparent reason in 1992, perhaps due to the financial difficulties faced by the company. The game was programmed by Booly's authors (Franck Cribier and Marc Cordier) and featured the 5 Bizzy brothers, cowboys in search of wealth who embarked on the gold rush. They have to exploit several mines to extract the gold, and this requires organizing. Indeed, each of the 5 siblings has a specialty: engineer, dynamite-or, rail-layer, digger, boast. It will therefore be necessary to make maximum use of their capacities for a limited period of time while ridding ourselves of the bugs that populate the mines. In short, an interesting cross between Diggers and The Lost Vikings.

423744.overview: Boulderdash 3D is a Boulderdash Clone in FPS mode, a 1996 demo game by Szymon Ulatowski. Originally intended for commercial use, it was never finished.

423755.overview:
Episode 1: Get Out Of My Stations
Episode 2: Tower in the Fountain of Sparks

423776.overview: Berek 2000 is a tag play for up to 4 players. At the beginning "berek" is chosen randomly or through eliminations. It can be set in game options as well. Eliminations base on the fast finding the exit from eliminations level. Exits are 3, randomly set at the level. The player which stays as last one becomes "berek" in a real game. To not to be "berek" one player have to collide with another player, then the next one is the one. The new "berek" will be frozen for a few seconds, to allow escaping from it. In the center of the screen every player has the time counter. When it'll reach the upper border, then the game is to end. When the player is "berek" in this moment, he loses the game. The time counters can work synchonically or only for "berek".

423943.overview: intended to be a pixel-perfect/arcade-perfect Bombjack game, Old Bob released a version for testing on multiple Amiga platforms. Not that version...the other one! This one was never completed.

423980.overview: A strategy demo game created by Dirk Hasse and released in 1990 as freeware.

423982.overview:
Then I wanted to make a Defender of the Crown type of game, which is entirely possible with CanDo, but along the way it turned into Hannibal, when I found and used a map of Europe instead of Britain. But making a Strategy Demo was boring, and slow, and it would take way too long. So after discovering that I could make trails appear by accident, I realised this would make for a much more interesting high speed battle experience. The whole thing took about a month to make. 

 HOW TO BEAT THE ENEMY:

* Move close to an enemy and try to anticipate the square where it will move next. Move there.

* Squash the enemy and watch for another to respawn.

* Move closer to the enemy base, and take out the next enemy.

* Try to kill an enemy within 1 square of the enemy base, so you can move to the enemy base square next.

* When the base is destroyed, the 06 on the panel will drop to 05, and this shows your progress.

* If you land on a base square but nothing happens, press fire to skip a turn, to force the attack. 
 
The A.I will run away from the player, and so the score for A.I  is worth a lot more.  On Difficulty 1, there are no re-revivals. With Difficulty 2 and 3, the enemies revive in a set pattern on a set number of clicks/movements.  Sometimes several will revive together, although if the enemies were already alive, it wont respawn them. The Difficulty will eventually stop reviving enemies after a set number of clicks/movements, to stop the game becoming boring.

423997.overview: A shareware blackjack game by Zymotic Software, released in 1994. Get a collection of cards equaling 21 or closer to 21 than the dealer gets and win the pot!

424001.overview: A Battleship board game created by Steve Berry in Forth and released as freeware in 1988. "Sink ships" in American. With numerous new features. Just try it out...

424116.overview: A single player freeware role playing game created by ZSoft in 1998. Black Dawn IX: Workbench Invasion was published as freeware by German PD publisher Berliner Spielekiste (Berlin PD) as number SK1294.

424772.overview:
Welcome to Brilliant English!
In this program there is the possibility of training in eight different areas of the English language. Exercises are available of varying degrees of difficulty and you can choose one that suits you well. I hope that this program facilitates your studies in English. 
 
ENTER YOUR CHOICE
Prepositions
The vocabulary
Find the shape
A or AN?
Plural
Shining

440082.overview:
Your Mission: To retrieve the PK430 secret fighter plane stolen from your country and fly it back. There is no time to weigh our options, you must drive deep into enemy territory to recover the PK430 using the military’s most advanced land vehicle, capable of leaping high into the air at the push of a button. This is a one-way trip pilot, you’re coming back home in that fighter jet, or not at all.

Gameplay: Breakthru is a horizontal shoot 'em up where the player controls an armed vehicle, with the first button shooting the main gun while the second button is used for jumping. During levels the player must face off against enemy soldiers, turrets and vehicles, as well as various obstacles along the way. The player can run over drums and crates, while other obstacles will cause the player to lose a life, so you must either avoid or jump over them. 

Keep a look out for power-ups that give access to a powerful three-way gun, but time will be limited and you must jump high to obtain them, else they will be captured by the enemy.

Score extra lives on 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k and 100k

P - Pause/Un-pause game

M - Return to title screen 

ESC - Quit to desktop from the title screen.

440548.overview: This is Barrel game for Amiga i have built from a Demo in Scorpion Engine by Erik and compiled by me, I am calling this released but it is far from ready to play. At this point you can maneuver around the screen, jump, shoot and destroy barrels. And that is it.

443995.overview:
Your aim is to collect as many easter eggs as possible as fast as possible! So clearly the path you take is important!

You control a rabbit, bouncing around a classic Amiga Boing-Ball, and aside from collecting eggs theres some other things to watch out for:

	Energy Drink - Rabbit will hop faster for a short time allowing you to complete the level quicker. Be careful... it might be too fast!

	Bomb - Avoid at all costs! This will kill your rabbit and end the game. 

This game is written using AMOS, and the full source code is included with the download! And yes, I took some inspiration for this game from a certain hedgehog themed bonus level.

446396.overview: A freeware AMOS game and sequel to the first Boing game, a scrolling screen platformer where you must bounce and spring over dangers and impediments to grab all the goodies and get to the exit. The AIM of the game is to collect all stars and get to the exit. The last two levels are broken. So you must skip a star else the game will crash. You can also get stuck and the score counter resets for every level.

446446.overview: Arrow Dynamic Soft in 1996 released this game in two versions, a demo version and the full Licenseware version. The game is a cross between Scorched tanks and M*A*S*H/Ant Wars. Some might call it a Worms Clone but they would be less correct. It is a game for two players only, it cannot be played solo. The full version allows all 9 rounds of play, selectable start energy and allows use of Worms custom levels. The full version also shows the player name above the battle Beasties heads, 5 custom levels and 4 built-in levels and an HD installer.

447021.overview: Battaglia Navale is a very popular pencil and paper game all over the world.

447100.overview: A freeware SEUCK shooter created by Steve Winkler in 1991. Fly the Batwing over Gotham City and fight villains and clean the Joker's filth from the streets. Steve Winkler is a German Amiga art creator and game dabbler who is a member of the Commodore Amiga Society of Montgomery, CASM.

447104.overview: A SEUCK based shooter written by Marcus and released in 1992. Space Zombie Makers have taken over the town and if you don't want to be a zombie you'll need to fight! Dodge and take out birds, bullies and bulldogs as you make your way through Springfield and try to get to the next level. Dodge ninja stars, banana flingers and every horror this town has set in your path.

448758.overview:
Brainstorm is a straight conversion of the game Concentration (also known as Memory). There is a set of 54 cards flipped on their back so every card looks the same. On the flip-side, there are 26 pairs with different motives. The players (in turn) flip over two cards each while trying to find a pair. When a pair is found, it is removed from the table. The goal is to find more pairs than the opponent.

This version features six card decks and the option to play alone (with the goal to have the least turns as possible), against the AI (nine difficulty levels) or against another person.

448763.overview: The Tüfftelspiel play\puzzle game, written entirely in assembler, was published in the Amiga Fun by CT Verlag in 1993. Something fun to rack your brains on.

448975.overview: Backgammon Royal is based on the board game Backgammon. Of course this program knows all the rules, including doubling cubes or beaver. Besides the variable difficulty level (two settings), the main feature is the tactics editor in which the player can "train" the AI. For new players, the game can highlight the possible moves and has some decent music

448982.overview:
A deluxe backgammon commercial game created by Armin Niggemann, with music by T. Kinnunen, O. Gollanek and A. Stelzer. The game supported one or two players and came out in 1993. Backgammon is a dice game whose history dates back a long time and whose country of origin is unknown. India or China is very likely, because we got most of our games from there. 

For example, there is an old Indian game called Parcheesi. In Parcheesi, as in backgammon, the player must first bring all of his pieces to the home field before he can play them. In both games, a single uncovered piece is a vulnerability and can be thrown off the board by the opponent. Excavations in Pompeii have revealed carved backgammon motifs in many villas. Some medieval cathedrals in Germany contain backgammon depictions in the church decorations.
In the Middle Ages, at least 25 different backgammon variants, then called tabulae, were played in different parts of Europe. 

From the 14th century onwards, English history and literature increasingly refer to tables, the direct precursor of modern backgammon. 

Until now, only the aristocracy was allowed to play, which forced the common people to play in secret. For example, books were found that were disguised backgammon games. In the middle of the 17th century, the Danish King Christian IV and the Swedish Chancellor Axel Oxenstierna even played backgammon for the customs rights in the Öresund (the strait between Denmark and Sweden). Become a part of the history and enjoy a game!

448985.overview: A one or two player backgammon game written in AmigaBASIC, included as part of the AMIGA POWER PACK compilation in 1987.

449007.overview: Nr. 80 in the Courbois Software Amiga series, this Dutch language version of the game appears to be for two players.  Find as many unique Dutch words as possible from the jumbled letters in the grid.

449146.overview: A billiards like game for one or two players is included on Amiga Spiele 1 and Amiga Extra 3.  BLIFF is a mixture of billiards and golf. Alone or with another player, the aim is to get balls the pool table after a carom. The only thing that can disturb your concentration is the computer fan...

449356.overview: A German-language text adventure with still pictures by Rudi\Rudolf Stember in 2020. It was published by Amiga Fun (Germany), Issue 11/90 (Nov 90). The English translation of game title: "Blood Thirst" or "Bloodlust". Somewhat similar to Holiday Maker/Stadt der Loewen, but a budget version of them. The most challenging part is escaping the killer in the maze, you might want to draw a map for that.

449640.overview:
With Bundesliga 3000 you can not only manage the Bundesliga, but also create tables for all other sports that are played in a Bundesliga-like format. 

Bundesliga 3000 creates clear and meaningful tables, taking home and away games and goal difference into account. Catch-up dates, yellow/red cards, sending offs, list of goalscorers, team line-ups, spectator numbers...
With the convenient printing routines you can output all evaluations to any printer. With Bundesliga 3000 you always have everything you need to know about the Bundesliga under control!

449703.overview: Blowout & Cosmic Alphabet is a compilation of games, developed by Greg Abernethy and Martin Fitzgibbons and published by Rush, which was released in Australia in 1992.

449737.overview: "Battle At Sea’, this mouse-driven strategy game, which runs on all Amigas with at least one Megabyte of memory on board, is giftware: the user may therefore decide for himself what he or she gives the author as compensation. This is an expansion of the idea of Battleship crated using AMOS pro in 1994.

449738.overview: A two player shareware billiard and other cue games including basic pool and snooker games. Created by Mikko Makela in 1993 using AMOS. The goal is to pocket all your balls and then the black one.

449742.overview: As a magic ball you have to navigate the labyrinths to the burial chamber of the pharaoh to protect him and save the treasures from grave robbers. The path to get there is not easy. Keys must be found to open doors, and also the gates to the burial chamber do not open so easily. Puzzles and tasks await. An exciting labyrinth game from Roy Schneider released as freeware in 1991.

449755.overview: A freeware version of Baloonacy, written in AMOS by Darkside PD (John Snowball) and released in 2001. It was available on The Assassins #77. Use the switch to open the exit then get your balloon to the exit without getting popped and before time runs out. Balloonacy is inspired by the arcade game Crazy Balloon, although it is not a direct port. Move your balloon to tough a switch to open the exit then make your way to the exit. Avoid force fields that go on and off and moving enemies. Do not tough the walls or the closed exit or you will pop. Do not dilly-dally as there is a time limit.

449764.overview: A single player, Czech-language freeware shooter from Legion Software Alliance in 1997. It is something of a Space Invaders clone written in AMOS. Our socialist homeland was insidiously attacked by fighters. imperialist bombers. But there is still hope. A hero has been found in our people's democratic army who will voluntarily fight for world peace and the rights of all working people with a weapon in hand! With the Soviet Union forever! (or at least until November)

449767.overview:
A single-player freeware strategy game paradoxically published in Amiga Classix Gold, the game was created in 1995 by Newline International Software. The game's name refers to the siege and it is a popular German board game with a version even being put out by Milton Bradley at one point. Two players compete, with the attackers outnumbered by the defenders. The defenders protect a fortress with two officers. The attackers must box in the officers before their forces are weakened. 
 
   The Belagerungs spiel was probably the most popular war game of the 1800s. A descendant of Fox and Geese, it is played on a cruciform game board: the upper arm represents a fortress and the other three the field before it. The two players’ forces are unequal: two officers defend the fortress against many attacking rebels. The rebels must box in the officers before their superior forces are weakened by capture.

449786.overview: in Blackboard Math 1.1, an educational freeware game written in BASIC by D. Stockton in 1987, there are four levels of difficulty of math problems for early math learners.

449813.overview: Number 16 in a 20 game series of BoulderDash style Emerald Mine games from De Bond, created with the Emerald Mine Editor and sold commercially via the Emerald Web of the EMC:  Emerald Mine Club in Holland in 1994.

449880.overview:
Exercise your Amiga's mouse in this fast-paced arcade-style game. Are you ready for 16 levels of arcade action? If you are, pop in your Resource Disk and double-click on tine Break Down icon. This Breakout-style game features unique background patterns and blocks with special powers. And it's our first game to include a full blown musical score.

There are three kinds of blocks In Break Down: standard, wall, and special. You progress through the levels by using your paddle to knock a ball into every standard brick on the screen. The standard blocks are translucent red, green, and yellow. Wall bricks are solid gray and can never be broken. Power blocks each give you a different special benefit.

Red power blocks give you a second paddle which floats above your main paddle. This paddle gives you an extra chance to strike the ball. It also provides you with a quick way to change the trajectory of the ball if you get into a rut with the single paddle.

Each purple power block gives you an extra paddle. You start Break Down with three paddies. The number of paddles in reserve is shown in the scoring box on the right side of the screen. You can have a maximum of five paddles in reserve, although only three are shown in the box. You lose a paddle whenever the ball goes off the bottom of the screen. When you lose your last paddle, the game ends.

Striking a green power block completes a level despite the number of standard bricks left on the screen. Note that striking these blocks may cause you to miss out on other special blocks which might be available. They may also prevent you from obtaining extra points.

Yellow power blocks slow down your ball. The change takes effect the next time the ball strikes your paddle.

There are three types of blue power blocks. Each is worth the number of points it is labeled with. 

Created by Rhett Anderson and Randy Thompson and published as a coverdisk for COMPUTE!'s Amiga Resource - Volume 2 Number 3 in 1990-06, COMPUTE! Publications

449982.overview:
Visit the zoo, feed the animals.
Bethany's Zoo! Is a program Robert W. Benjamin made for his (then) 5 year old daughter, who just happens to be named Bethany. There are lots of different animals to visit, and some can even be fed. Each animal has a speaker on it's fence, pressing the speaker gives a verbal story or bit of fact about the animal. Written in AMOS and released as freeware in 1997.

450022.overview: A one or two player, freeware Bandy management game by Torbjorn Lindquist that was partially unfinished. Bandy is a big sport in Sweden. It is played on a field as big as a soccer field. It is played on ice with a ball at the size of about 2 inches and curved sticks. There is 11 11 players in each team and 3 substitutes. But in this early version, the substitutes isn't implemented yet. Th The teams are Swedish, and the names to. I hope you won't get any trouble with Swedish characters, if so, please tell me and I try to do something about it.

450052.overview: A freeware Minesweeper style game that could be played from the workbench, created by Rob Janssen in 1997.

450053.overview:
You may already know that the boomerang is a lethal weapon. But the odds are that you don't realize just how lethal it can be. Once you play Boomerang, a great two player arcade game for your Amiga, you'll know— and you'll never forget the lesson.  
 
Boomerang takes place in a cold and deadly arena. Besides the walls, there's just you, your opponent, your boomerang, and his or her boomerang. Although the requirements for the real-life version of Boomerang are only two boomerangs, mortals playing. the game on an Amiga will need two joysticks.

To play, double-click the Boomerang folder to open it, then double-dick on the game's icon to get started. When the game screen appears, plug in two joysticks. If you wish to copy the game to anottier disk, be sure to drag the entire folder to the other disk.

Choose Your Arena

Boomerang is typically played in a maze of randomly placed walls, but when you first load the game you have the option of playing in an empty pit If you'd like to play in this pit, press Return. Otherwise, press the space bar. Each press of the bar wilt place you into a new room with randomly generated walls. When you're satisfied with the playing field, press Return.  
 
Published as a coverdisk in COMPUTE!'s Amiga Resource - Volume 2 Number 1 (1990-02) from COMPUTE! Publications.

450087.overview: Use the left and right cursor keys to move the balls to the crystals and collect'em up! Avoid the holes! A game by Todd Lewis of LunchHour Software and playable on the workbench. This game was a coverdisk in 1990 and also published by Amiga Club Systems.

450148.overview: A version of the  Shanghai solitaire tile game created by Thomas Behrend and published as a cover disk on Amiga Special (media GmbH) in 1991. The game was created in Amiga BASIC and it allowed one or two players, which you don't see in this game often. The game play involves 144 tiles, each depicting different images, which have to be removed by matching them into pairs. The tiles are arranged in a grid pattern, which is higher near the center. A tile can only be removed if it has no tile next to it on at least one side.

450244.overview: A freeware, AMOS tic-tac-toe\nautghts and crosses game for one player from 1991, with a special magical twist. Released as part of Hobbs Games Vol I and in APD254.

450263.overview:
This  game  is a variation on the old bat and ball game.  The difference here  is  that instead of knocking a ball back to your opponent, the aim is  to  stop  the balls hitting the boundary on your side of the screen. The  balls  appear  several  at  a  time  and  move across the screen at differing  speeds  so that you have to dash from one end to the other to
hit  them.  If you miss, you lose a life, if you hit lots, you get extra lives.   There  are very many different options you can use to make each game  different.  These include speed and different game screen choices, e.g.  vertical game with balls coming from top and/or bottom, horizontal game etc.  An interesting game from Graham who has several others in the
library.  Created by Graham Lund and released as freeware in 1994.

450264.overview:
A freeware AMOS based game from Jurriaan Knol of Stealth Software. Reaction and skill are required! Before the
Background of the Kuwait conflict becomes the American Stand.  Daghran attacked with Iraqi rockets. Of course, these must be recognized and shot down - but be careful, not all of them are shown by the radar! Use left mouse button to end the game.

450265.overview: Published as part of the Amiga Special compilation along with Jumper, The Dungeon, Waltermat and Sculptor, this action puzzle feels very much like a variant of a BoulderDash clone.

450291.overview: Black Jack Trainer is a freeware game from Peter Cartwright in 1991 has lots of options and is a nice implementation of Black Jack. The main options include a help system and the ability to load, save and test various strategies and staking. If you like Black Jack or want to try and learn how to play it then get this disc.  The game was written in AMOS.

450292.overview: An action game by Josh Addison aka Monkeyfluids back in 1992  when he was 16 using AMOS. Can you get Herbert home and save his village? Jump the baddies and spikes to get to the bottom of the third level.

450293.overview:
This  is  the latest addition from Roger North.  This is a platform game where the aim is to bound upwards to reach an exit hole at the top of the  screen. Not as simple as it sounds! Between you and the exit are platforms, gaps appear randomly as the platforms move across the screen.

You have to jump up through these gaps to reach the top exit.  There are no meanies on level one,  so you can get the feel of the game before progressing onto the higher levels where you have to avoid these beasts as well as trying to get to the top of the screen!  An AMOS based freeware game by Roger North in 1992 and distributed by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) and later by The Assassins.

450370.overview: A freeware AMOS game by Tony Kingsmill, created in 1995. Choose from 3 level of difficulties and attempt to guess the word in this Hangman style game. For every guess you miss, a bottle falls off the wall. If they all fall, you lose the game.

450444.overview: A German-language shareware basketball sport management game created by BauerSoft (Jens Neubauer) in 1996. The demo version of the game was published on 2 disks on Berliner Spielekiste as SK #1002. The full version was published by Berliner Spielekiste/Berlin PD as SK GOLD #13. In 2016 APC/TCP was able to publish all 5 Bauersoft games on the cover CD of Amiga Future #121. All Bauersoft games were developed with CanDo 2.0 - 2.5. Manage players, keep an eye on the injury list, train your players and make sure you have a court to play on. Advertising, transportation, laborers and travel all fall on your shoulders, you are the sixth man in the game and your role is key!!

450446.overview:
Biorytm is a Biorythm program for the Amiga created by Grzegorz Szymczak and Krzystof Pichlak in 1994. Biorhythms are a cross between technology and astrology except using your body as the effective heavens, it purports to help you track  biological cycles that some believe affect a person's daily life, moods, and behavior. The theory of biorhythms is considered pseudoscientific, and many (all sane) scientists are skeptical of it.  
 
The length of each cycle is the same for everyone, but the timing of highs and lows varies based on birth date. Some (the dupes) believe that biorhythms can help people plan their lives around their cycles. However, studies have found that the predictive power of biorhythm charts is no better than chance.

450483.overview:
Brain Fodder is a set of English language learning programs. * Funtest - consists in making a word from the letters in three rows.

-    Scrabble - is a classic scrabble game.
-    Speech Snatch - checks the correct pronunciation.
-    Puzzle - consists in arranging a sentence from scattered puzzles.

450509.overview: A shareware billiards game created by Stefan Salewski using Oberon in 1989. Play a game of skill and physics and rule the felt

450552.overview: An action puzzle in the vein of BoulderDash, created by Wolfgang Schulz in 1989. You start the game with 4 Rockfords and must gather all the diamonds on the screen while avoiding a boulder to the head. Make your way through the underground by moving stones and destroying goths.

450574.overview: A 1990 freeware puzzle game created by Joachim Scholz and published by Spielekiste (Berlin PD).

450598.overview: A single player black jack game created it 1990, it would be later released as part of the "50 Great Games" compilation by Wicked Software in 1991. Choose house rules or number of decks in the shoe and get playing. Blackjack pays one and a half times the bet on the first hand only. Dealer hits on 16 or less. No win on a tie. Can split if cards iqual on first hand, can double the bet for one card on the first hand only.

451356.overview: A full screen Arkanoid-esque clone by Climent Corde with full mouse control.

451435.overview:
Battle for Wesnoth is a turn-based fantasy strategy game. Various races - humans, elves, dwarfs, drakes and undead - and various factions battle for the control of the land of Wesnoth in various eras.

The strategic gameplay is similar to games such as Master of Monsters and Warsong. The players, represented in game as high-level commander units, recruit new units, who then fight, advance in experience and eventually turn to another units.

There's both a multiplayer mode, which typically involves wiping out the enemy (or at least their commander). For single player games, there are several campaigns as well as ability to play multiplayer mode against the computer. Also included is a map editor and a scripting language to construct new campaigns.

451500.overview: An Arkanoid shareware clone with many new features. Choose between 3 level sets, has multiball, fire, brickthrough, ball saving guard, many falling object. Has bump\tilt motion by pressing spacebar will modify the path of the ball.

451550.overview: A single player, freeware board game from Andre Wüthrich and St. Gallen in 1987. It was published in several freeware collections, including by Spielekiste (Berlin PD). In Barricade you and your opponents race your 5 tokens from your home base to the finish along wide and/or narrow paths. You may pick up "barricades" if you land on them exactly with the DIE ROLL and move them to any space above the first row to block everyone's move. No one can move past a barricade unless it is landed on exactly. Has a built-in board\level editor.

451581.overview:
An AMOS based shareware game from Steve Hovelroud and Lindsay Whipp in 1993. Baron Baldric receives a deputation from the Rim Village asking to rid the Lazarine Tower from the evil monsters inside and to restore the peace.  Baron listens and decides to enter the "Mystic Towers" and complete the villager's requests.

Your job is to rid the towers of the monsters plus destroy a Monster Generator in each tower.

451582.overview: A four-player worm\lightcycle game by Weird Kondition (Serenity, Grafton) in 1995. Avoid the tail of your fellow players and your own, live the longest without intersecting a line and you win!

451583.overview:
A shareware text based strategy management game from Scherzsoftware (Adrian Jaglarz) in 1993. Excellent economic and trading simulation. This slightly limited demo version is about buying and selling freight; work robots and transport ships also play an important role. Who will lead their company to the top? - Shareware for the full version. 
 
An entertaining business simulation, in which the companies "Universal Beans", "United Beans" and 'Super Beans' fight for power. How usually it is about the most effective possible Sale of goods, although the main threat here not from the competition, but from above in the form mighty tomatoes. If you want to know more, you will become a frequent Beans player.

451635.overview: A freeware puzzle game by Digital Prophets (Chris Haynes, Alan Taylor) for one or two players, created in AMOS in 1992 and published by  Nordlicht Spiele 09-06. Touch the matching blocks together to destroy them, leave no blocks un-exploded.

451641.overview: A freeware game by Colin Adams, created in 1991 in C. It was released by CAM and in Assassins Disk 191. The instructions are simple: Blow everything to pieces. Joystick up and down to increase and decrease altitude. right and left to rotate clockwise or counter clockwise. Spacebar and Backspace to increase and decrease velocity. P and U to pause and unpause. Blast it all!

451642.overview: A four-player shareware party game, set the variables for the environment and adjust your character setup as desired then take out your rivals\friends and have a blast. Created by Team 4 and a half this is an inverted shooter as you do NOT shoot, but there are bullets already flying around and you can push your rivals into them. Win a set by eliminating all of them.

451643.overview: A shareware puzzle game created by Hermann Kuntsch and released 1989.

451644.overview: A shareware shooter from Consix for two players in vs mode with top and bottom split screen. Released in S p i e l e k i s t e # 402 in 1993.

451646.overview:
A freeware collect'em up game by Oliver Wagner in 1994. Collect all the pills before entering the next level of Desastrous [sic] Castle. Find chests that contain valuable things or bonuses, use teleporters and gather keys, which can only be used once. Activate electric doors with the buttons. Ghosts fear loud noises, so use grenades when you need to.  
 
You are Pacman, You start in a maze, and like Pacman, your task is to collect all the Dots to open the exit

What makes this Game more unique than that, is you have pickups with question marks on them, along with keys which can open other areas in the map for you to collect either more dots, bonuses and even more keys sometimes

Additionally, you have BOMBS, which can be used to blow up walls, and enemies what venture around in a quite random fashion, chase after you to try and kill you

On some levels there are doorways which can be opened by a button as well, houses which work as teleporters, sending you to another part of the map, and RIP Gravestones which appear to do nothing

Once you have collected all the dots, the exit will open, which initially is shown as a Green door with the word EXIT written on it, once activated it looks like an open door that you must proceed towards to exit and complete the level

There are sound effects which occur for dot munching, specials pickup and there is a musical tone at the end of each completed level

451648.overview: On Valentine's day in 1994, Alain Ceccato created BCS or the Bonhomme Construction Kit version 2.3, so you could make your own good man, in French, of course.  Created using CanDo.

451656.overview: A German-language adventure game published as Shareware by Axolottisoft in 1993.

451668.overview: Basic crosshair freeware shooter with from Top Sprite Software in 1994. The game is for a single player and a rather distracting scroller at the bottom. The goal is to blast all the bouncing bunnines. All levels had the same background graphics. What changed was the allotted amount of ammunition, the number of bunnies to be blasted, and special items like dynamite. The game ends when you run out of ammunition. Available on Spielekiste Nr. 393 and Assassins Vol. 97.

451671.overview: A freeware virtual friend. I am virtual Bertie and I may want to be your friend, if you are desperate enough. Let's talk! With virtual friends who needs mates? Stay and chat with me for hours and hours. Eliza ain't got nothing on me! A game for ONE player, who needs more?

451676.overview: A freeware German-language, Black Box workbench game created by Stephan Ilaender. Blackbox rules are well established. There is an 8x8 grid which contains several atoms hidden in it. Your job is to find the location of all of the atoms by projecting rays from the side of the box and observing what happens. If a ray directly hits an atom it will be absorbed. Rays that pass within one box of an atom will be reflected. After you have fired enough rays, you can venture a guess as to an atom's location. To help prevent random guessing, you lose points for a ray that completely misses an atom or an incorrect guess about the atom's location, and gain points for rays that are absorbed or reflected and for a correct guess.

451680.overview: A shareware game featuring a very simple fruit\slot machine with 3 reels, created and published by Tom Wysocki in 1995 using AMOS.

451692.overview:
Biplane Blitz, an arcade shooter game by Milt Henderson came out in 1995. It features dual playfields with double scrolling. The plane is controlled with the joystick, with it set to rise on the joystick being pushed forward. The fire button controls the machine gun. Pulling back on the joystick while holding the fire button down will release a bomb. If you prefer aviation style controls, they can be reversed during the the opening title screen.  
 
the main objective of the game is to destroy your foes symbol of his air superiority. But before you can fly this final mission, you must prove yourself by flying increasingly difficult missions. When you have gained enough points you will be allowed to fly the next mission in succession, and then eventually to the final mission.

451694.overview: In Black Box 1.1 by Tim Kemp there is an 8x8 grid which contains several atoms hidden in it. Your job is to find the location of all of the atoms by projecting rays from the side of the box and observing what happens. If a ray directly hits an atom it will be absorbed. Rays that pass within one box of an atom will be reflected. After you have fired enough rays, you can venture a guess as to an atom's location. To help prevent random guessing, you lose points for a ray that completely misses an atom or an incorrect guess about the atom's location, and gain points for rays that are absorbed or reflected and for a correct guess. If you get stumped, you can end the game early and peek at the location of all atoms.

451702.overview: Place the bombs you have in order to get the red fruit, use bombs to gain access to walled or rocked blocked areas. An action and logic game from Olof Astrand, made in 1993 with AMOS.

451705.overview: A freeware game created by Cluster (André Wichmann) in 1990 to give people a puzzle to solve while assembling\compiling the programming they are working on. Try to match the numbers on the sample box, when you increase the numbers in any square, the ones around it go up. This forces you to plan in an inverted way and think steps ahead.

451706.overview: An AMOS based, freeware quiz game created in 1991 by Michael Flad. Brainy v1.10 is an entertaining knowledge game in the style of "Trivial Pursuit" for up to 6 players. The aim of the game is to complete the 6 "knowledge corners" (e.g. sports & entertainment, art & literature, entertainment, etc.) and finally land on the top left starting field. In the finale, at least 3 of the 6 questions asked must be answered correctly. With question editor.

451707.overview: A freeware, German-language game from Jörg Woyke and Meik Woyke, with version 2.5c releasing in 1992. A challenging quiz on literature! After up to three clues, you have to guess a title or author. Listing available from the author as Charityware, send anything and they would send you the game code. Released in S p i e l e k i s t e # 136.

451715.overview: Bosseln is a game of skill in which two players have to try to throw wooden balls as far as possible in a landscape. The throwing technique rather than luck determines the distance of the throw. The game requires 1 MB. Author: R. Werner in 1991 and is freeware.

451716.overview: A 1995 shareware Boulderdash clone by Steve Yrjänä also known as BulderECS. BulderECS: It would be nice if the diamonds were really lying around and you just had to collect them. But it's not quite that easy: you can still dig through the sand quite easily, but if a stone falls on your head, it really hurts. So much so that you need a new character. So you do need to be a bit careful when digging for profit. But the beetles and other vermin that cross your path are really nasty. You can only overcome them with cunning and trickery to get to the level exit unscathed. A fine new version of the well-known Boulder Dash! Shareware. - From OS 2.0. In 2024 an AGA version was released called Bulder AGA.

451987.overview: A freeware two player board game Abalone. the aim is to push all your opponents marbles off the field. On your turn, you can move one, two, or three of your marbles one space in any direction.      You can push your opponent's marbles if you have more marbles in your line than they do. For example, you can push one or two marbles with three marbles, or one marble with two marbles. You can only push marbles into an empty space or off the board. When your column is next to and in line with fewer marbles from your opponent, you have a Sumito advantage. In this position, you can push columns with fewer marbles in line. You can't push marbles that are sandwiched between your own marbles.

451996.overview: Breaking Out is an action game similar to Breakout or Arkanoid by Carsten Hund, published in Amiga Extra Nr. 5: Spiele by Markt & Technik in 1988 along with MegaMind and Wikinger II. The aim is to clear stubborn stone walls with a ball. If difficulty levels are not enough for you, you can create new levels at any time with the editor.

452097.overview: A freeware, workbench enabled minesweeper clone from Olivier Fabre in 1999.

452099.overview: in this arcade action game by Bob Akerberg, your spaceship has been caught in the gravitational pull of a black hole. You can rotate 360 degrees, fly forwards and fire to activate your breaks, but the black hole gravitational pull will continue to pull you towards the screen center and death. The player gets points for bumping enemy ships into the black hole as they try to do the same to you.

452286.overview:
This is a demake of the 2020 game Beyond a Steel Sky. This version is written with Scala MM400 and it's a point and click game, very similar to the game Myst. 

Set ten years after the events of the 1994 video game Beneath a Steel Sky, you assume the role of Robert Foster as he finds himself returning to Union City on the hunt for a kidnapped child, only to learn that the city's new utopia state is not what it appears to be.

Beyond a Steel Sky is a video game developed and published by Revolution Software. This is a port of that game. Solve the puzzles and find a way into Union City and solve the crime.

452296.overview: A four player board game that can be played on the workbench by Michal Szafranski in 1997. This version of the board game comes with dozens of possible board configurations to choose. The game is packed with strategy and designed for 2 to 4 players. The most fun to be had is when players do not try to spare each other's feelings, so be prepared for some exciting conflict at family game night! Barricade originated from Germany in 1959, and was called Malefiz at the time.

452303.overview: A freeware Arkanoid style game made by Jeroen Knoester of Power Programs made in 1998 written in AMOS. Sadly, it only really worked smoothly on an Amiga with at least a 68020 processor, but I hope you enjoy it. If any level is too hard just use the included level editor to make your life easier. Bugfixes released on Aminet makes it appear multiple separate games with this name were released, in fact the slightly later release is just a bugfix to the original. As usual remove the bricks while keeping the ball in play as long as possible. Missing the ball loses a life.

454143.overview: Boulder Bash is a  single player Boulder Dash clone created by Robert Wille in 1991 and was part of the BoulderDash Clones Compilation.

454144.overview: A revamp of BoulderDash for the Amiga created by the originator of BoulderDash, Peter Liepa along with Levas Vabolis, together known as Savel Software who released this as a fully Open Source initiative in 1995. Called variously, Boulder Dash!, Boulder Dash 2.x and the Boulder Engine, this version didn't spark quite the enthusiasm as hoped as Emerald Mines was already very well accepted in the Amiga community. However, enjoy the fully open source code and editor written in C!

454178.overview:
Pilot your ship through three stages of enemy waves and face the final boss. Loop back to beginning after defeating the boss and go for a high score. This was the Bitwise Brains entry for AmigaJam 2024. 


Controls:
Joystick or arrow keys for movement
Joystick Button 1 or spacebar to shoot
Joystick Button 2 or B for special
P to pause
ESC to quit


Hints:
Player ship moves faster when not firing.
Collecting pickups when a level is at maximum rewards points.
Player starter weapon does the most damage.
End of stage points bonus for enemies destroyed and special remaining.
End of stage points penalty for number of times player died.
Only one powerup can be on screen at any time.
Loop iteration multiplies point values.

454515.overview: A single player platformer by Michael Taupitz released as part of the Berlin Games Box and featured in Amiga Future magazine and Spielekiste 204. Grab the diamonds and avoid the baddies.

455746.overview: To take down a zombie, as is known, you have to hit it in the head... there is no other way. To do this you will find various weapons but be careful, ammunition is limited. However, you will find crates containing ammo around the city.

455853.overview: "You are wondering if this is the correct path to a forgotten cave rumored to be filled with gold beyond your deepest imagination!"

455969.overview:
In a world almost devoid of floppy disks, an evil overlord has been hoarding the last of these precious floppies!
This small game was made as a tribute and gesture of appreciation for AmigaBill's amazing contribution to the Amiga community.

457165.overview: transcode of Burger Time arcade version for 68000/020 amiga machines

459012.overview: Released 28 June 2025 4th in the Posadas 2025 Homebrew Games competition

459948.overview: A collection of Boulder Dash games made by various individuals/groups using the Amiga version of the Boulder Dash Construction Kit.

459991.overview:
Breach: Scenario Disk - The Serayachi Campaign contains additional levels and campaigh for Breach.

The first moon of Kiskismok is under Federated Worlds control, and they have allowed both Federated Worlds (FW) and United Democratic Planets (UDP) to establish research stations there, even turning a blind eye to the squatter colonies that have started turning up along the jungle and coastal areas of the moon.

When the Unification Talks failed, civil unrest among the squatter colonies rose sharply. Intelligence reports there are organized groups planning to form their own planetary government with military assistance from the UDP. Intelligence has concluded that the UDP will attempt to take control of the moon sometime in the next few days. Several squads of FW teams have been sent to the immediate area to respond if trouble breaks out.

461759.overview: Classic battle ship game with simple AI for AmigaOS 3.x.

461890.overview:
The Block Out playing pieces are created by combining the four elements of the ancient world (earth, fire, water, and wind) with five colors. Two players score points by placing these pieces into a grid of 13 columns and 8 rows, specifically when they manage to position two pieces with the same element and/or the same color side-by-side.

Published in the March 1990 AmigaMagazine OnDisk #10 and also in Assassins CD1 Ultimate Games.

461981.overview: The classic casino betting game, published in October 1994 in AmigaMagazine OnDisk #60.

462117.overview: Bonzo is on a space journey to destroy evil enemies on three different planets.

462792.overview:
On Monday 18th April, 1994 Brian Lara broke a cricketing record that had stood since 1958, long before Lara himself was born.

Lara's 375 for West Indies against England is the highest individual score ever recorded in a test match, beating Sir garfield Sobers' 365. In more than 12 hours at the crease he faced 536 balls and hit 45 boundaries.

Just weeks later, Lara was in record-breaking form once again, hitting 501 not out for Warwickshire against Durham, the highest score in first class cricket!

BRIAN LARA'S CRICKET allows you to get in on the action, controlling batting, bowling, and field placing, Spectacular graphics and authentic player statistics make this the most realistic cricket simulation ever!

How many records will you break this season?

462841.overview: A small puzzle game for Amiga computers, where you roll a blue blok through 24 levels of increasing difficulty.

469992.overview: Backflip Endless is a fast-paced, parkour-inspired endless runner game. With randomly generated obstacles, a steadily increasing speed, and enjoyable music, the game delivers a challenging, satisfying, and delightfully frustrating experience.

470000.overview: The silly robots have kidnapped Bernie and Dino, so Blue and Red have decided to zap the robots, stomp them into oblivion, and rescue their beloved pets!

470133.overview: A side scrolling game inspired by the likes of Commander Keen, walk to the right, shoot fire demons, don't die

472360.overview: This airplane shooter game, created in 1994 by Bart ter Haar

474066.overview: Player one will always move on the horizontal axis while player two will always move on the vertical axis. Pick the tile with the highest score or force your opponent to pick a lower score in the next turn! Thinking ahead is the key to win the game.

479026.overview: Apogee Software's Bio Menace (1993, MS-DOS) ported to the Commodore Amiga. All three episodes, complete and playable.

480149.overview: A Puzzle-Bobble / Bust-A-Move style bubble shooter.Game was written in AmiBlitz3 entirely with the help of AI

480281.overview: A first-person space combat game for the Amiga

480641.overview: A native AmigaOS port of Bobr Hopper, a hopping game: cross the roads, the rivers and the railway without being run over. Classic (endless) and Progression (levels with a finish line, a career and ranks), English and Polish, a beaver or a chicken.

480773.overview:
A collection of mini LCD games, featuring Amiga Bill! Follow one week in the life of Amiga Bill Winters, by competing in 9 events.

On Monday, Amiga Bill has been given an assignment to take head shots of a famous celeb. Guide Bill in his car from Tarrytown to New York, New York. Unpack the flight cases from the back of the van. Run around the set of Mr. Robert Nero, as the lights move in different places, to capture his best sides. On Tuesday, get back to the van and load up all of the boxes.

But wait! On Wednesday he gets a call to attend the Emmys in LA. Drive Bill to the airport. On Thursday Bill must collect all of the Emmys from the judges tables before they fall.

But Wait! Bill Gates and Bill Murray come after you. Fight one of them on Friday, and then on Saturday hire a rental car for a quick get-away, and drive back from LA to NY. On Sunday there is a marathon streaming session, with the boing-ball, beer, and Amiga Mom. If you complete this task, Amiga Bill gets to sleep for 2 hours. Good luck!

480935.overview: Breakline Rugby 5 is a native Amiga AGA sports prototype built around short, tactical matches. Carry the ball, link backward passes, send a teammate on a crossing run, and slide your defensive line toward the open side. Six touches turn possession over. A forward kick must be caught before it hits the ground.

481049.overview: Bubble Killer is a simple but increasingly challenging arcade shooting game where the objective is to achieve the highest score possible.You are positioned at the center of the screen, surrounded by an ever-growing threat. Bubbles appear around you and move towards your position. Your only defense is to shoot them before they reach you.

481310.overview:
Breathless is a first-person-shooter, where the player has to navigate various stages infested with enemies out to get them. The player has a status display at the bottom of the screen. It contains the current score, the remaining health and shield as well as energy and credits. Energy functions as a universal ammo stock, with each of the weapon depleting a certain amount. By picking up credits, the player can buy or upgrade weapons at computer terminals.

(A32 version)
Patch for Amiga AGA/RTG bringing some new sprites, performance optimizations, improved enemy AI, CD32 Pad support.

481364.overview: Baseline Rally is a native tennis game for the Amiga A500, 68000 and OCS. It runs with 512 KB chip RAM and no expansion. Startup selects PAL or NTSC. The game includes menus, help, pause, scoring, sound, an attract demo with player takeover, and a match celebration. Reboot after play is intentional.

BRUCE LEE - Amiga port of Kagesan's Sega Master System version (2015)
by Tim Kovack (2026)

Beauty and the Beast (1982) (Imagic)
1:1 conversion from IntelliVision to 68k Amiga

481632.overview: It's a game for the Amiga 500 (512k) inspired by Tempest arcade game (tube shooter genre), The game is completely free, I used AI, this is version 1.0.

481644.overview: Porting the MD port found here https://github.com/rester159/blacktiger_MD to Amiga 500/1200.

481791.overview: BUGGY BOY - the Commodore 64 version, on the Amiga

482177.overview:
This is the first game from the neogeo hardware/taito system B ported to the Amiga 1200 !
A native 680X0 assembly port, designed to take advantage of the AGA chipset and the Amiga 1200’s stock processor.

482283.overview: The NES version is graphically and sonically superior to the arcade game, that's why!

482285.overview: Take to the skies in Blue Max, the Atari 8-bit classic that puts you in the cockpit of a World War I biplane on a daring mission behind enemy lines! Strafe ground targets, bomb bridges, and battle enemy fighters as you swoop across the scrolling isometric landscape. Keep your nerve steady and an eye on your fuel gauge—you’ll need a timely landing to refuel and rearm before your next attack. Every bombing run brings another chance for glory—or a fiery end! For AGA Amigas with 2MB FastRAM.

482651.overview:
Poland, spring 1982. Martial law. Print the truth.

You have just been thrown out of university. Your grandfather is interned along with the town's whole opposition. That leaves you and your friends, starting from nothing, with an underground newspaper to publish, a bibuła.

Bibuła is a classic mouse-driven point & click adventure, written as new software for the Atari ST, the Amiga and DOS PCs. It was created as a teaching aid for history lessons, and you can simply play it as an adventure game.

482816.overview: Classic AMIGA naval combat game designed exclusively for Commodore Amiga systems, compatible with the Amiga 500 Plus and higher models (requiring at least ECS and 1 MB of Chip RAM).

482877.overview:
You are Elnur, an elite soldier of the United Defense Federation, stranded in the distant galaxy where the Banu al-Jann have established their new empire.

Armed with advanced weapons and experimental technology, you must fight your way through hostile planets, ancient temples, underground fortresses, alien cities, and enormous enemy spacecraft.
